Louisiana Cannabis & Hemp Research — Audited Final Report

Last audited: 28 October 2026. Original research date / source-access date: 25 October 2026, unless a source itself is dated otherwise. This file is the audit (Part 1) and the corrected rewrite (Part 2) in one self-contained HTML document. It opens offline. Tables wrap rather than cut off.

Read this first — what the audit did and did not do

This is a separate fact-checking pass. The auditor did not write the original report. Every factual claim in the original was checked section by section against primary sources only: Louisiana Revised Statutes and bill/Act pages on legis.la.gov, the Louisiana Administrative Code and Louisiana Register, the Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), the Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry (LDAF), the Board of Pharmacy (historic records), the Office of Alcohol and Tobacco Control (ATC), the Louisiana Department of Revenue, LSU AgCenter and Southern University Agricultural Center, the Governor's official bill actions, the Secretary of State for election results, official tribal government sources, and official parish, consolidated-government and city sites and codes. Nothing was confirmed from news, law-firm blogs, trade press or AI summaries. Where only a secondary source exists, the claim is marked Unverified.

Federal baseline — used as given, not re-audited. Scheduling is split: under a final rule at 91 FR 22714 (effective 28 April 2026), FDA-approved cannabis products and state-licensed medical marijuana are in Schedule III; all other marijuana, including all adult-use, remains Schedule I; the broader 2024 rescheduling proposal is NOT final. IRS §280E: Treasury has said rescheduling generally removes §280E as a bar for businesses no longer dealing in Schedule I/II substances (guidance forthcoming); adult-use activity remains fully subject to §280E. Hemp: Public Law 119-37 §781 takes legal effect 12 November 2026, but Public Law 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026 to only the provisions excluding cannabinoids that are not naturally produced or are synthesized; the full total-THC definition and 0.4 mg per container cap apply after 11 December 2026. USDA has delayed enforcement of the DEA-registered-laboratory hemp testing requirement until 31 December 2026. The federal medical-marijuana appropriations rider is in force through 11 December 2026. No federal cannabis banking law has been enacted. Any statement in the original contradicting this baseline has been corrected to match it. Louisiana state law still treats marijuana as Schedule I for state purposes (R.S. 40:964, Schedule I) — that state classification is not changed by the federal rule.

How the rewrite was built. The rewrite below keeps every section and all detail from the original. Only what the audit changed has been changed. Wrong or outdated figures have been replaced everywhere they appear in the main text; no outdated value is left standing as current, and no 'earlier research said X' note is left in the main text. Internal assembler scope notes that falsely said the combined file covered only one part, and internal 'parent agent' instructions, have been replaced with the combined-file scope — they were not report content. Earlier-run gap lists that appear inside the body are superseded by the Still Unverified list below; a resolved item that appears in a historical run note is history, not a live flag. Verify or Unavailable flags remain only on items still unresolved after this audit.

Limits of this audit, stated plainly. Some sources were form-gated, rendered only through a search index, or blocked by a script in the original research window, and some registries have no systematic sweep: LDH's registered consumable-hemp products database and in-state sponsor list, ATC's permit roster, and LDAF's licensee list have no confirmed downloadable file (see Still Unverified). Licence totals that no registry confirmed are not presented as registry-confirmed. A claim marked Unverified must not be treated as settled, and an absence of a located source must not be read as proof that a power, ban or operation does not exist.

PART 1 — AUDIT

Verdict counts (must sum to the number of rows audited): 85 rows audited — Confirmed 35, Corrected 31, Removed 4, Unverified 15. Sum: 85. Verdict key: Confirmed = a primary source opened in this audit supports the claim as written. Corrected = a primary source supports a different wording, figure or date, applied in the rewrite. Removed = wrong and no correct version was found in a primary source, or the claim is a proposal/stale figure presented as current law/count and has been removed as such. Unverified = only a secondary source exists, or the primary source could not be opened directly in this audit.

Internal contradictions resolved (headline decisions). (1) Satellite/location counts: the LDH table counted in this audit (10 base + 19 satellites = 29, 14 Oct 2026 crawl) prevails over the older June 2026 snapshot (17/27) and press figures (27, ~23, 22–28) — those are superseded snapshots, not live conflicts. (2) Lab list: Ceres (current LDH list) prevails over Orion (earlier snapshot at the same Baton Rouge address); Orion is removed as a current lab, and a rename/successor relationship is not asserted. (3) 7% fee distribution: the Disability Services Fund wording, as quoted in current R.S. 40:1046(H)(4)(c) text in a 2025 legis bill text, prevails over an Act 150 allocation proposal in legislative history; no further split is stated. (4) LDH hemp rule: the January 2026 final rule (LR 52:57) prevails over the May 2025 Notice of Intent text. (5) LDH product review: 60 business days (statute) prevails over a 15-day FAQ excerpt. (6) School-zone penalty: Act 305's 1-year/$1,000 cap applies only to the (C)(2) marijuana subset of the (A)(4) smoking/vaping trigger, not to every drug-free-zone violation, which remains under (D). (7) Gas-station ban: the narrow gasoline-authorisation rule prevails over a blanket 'gas stations/convenience stores banned' summary. (8) ATC fees: caps ($500 / $175) prevail over fixed-fee statements.

§1.6 / §7Consumable hemp definition / total-THC measurementCorrectedlegis.la.gov — Act 752 (HB 952) ; legis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1483'Consumable hemp product' = product derived from industrial hemp containing any cannabinoid, intended for consumption or topical use, including commercial feed, pet products and hemp floral material, excluding non-intoxicating THC-free products and hemp-fibre industrial products. 'Total THC' = any combination of THC, THCA, THC component, or any derivative; 'THC component' = any naturally occurring cannabinoid component of hemp. Industrial hemp itself = Cannabis sativa L. with total delta-9 THC ≤0.3% dry weight. This is not a simple delta-9-only or post-decarboxylation 0.877 formula in §1481.
§1.6 / §75 mg/serving, 40 mg/package — scopeCorrectedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1483(B)(6)For products OTHER than beverages and tinctures for human consumption: each serving ≤5 mg total THC, distinct/separate, package ≤40 mg total THC, child-resistant packaging. Nonedible products are NOT subject to those serving/package limits (§1483(B)(6)(d)). Do not apply 5/40 mg to beverages or tinctures.
§1.6 / §7Beverage rule ('5 mg per 12 oz minimum')Correctedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1483(B)(6)(b),(c)Correct: a single beverage serving shall NOT exceed 5 mg total THC AND shall NOT be less than 12 ounces; each serving in an individual tamper-evident container, distinct from other servings; a package ≤4 individual containers. Tincture: 1 mL serving, ≤1 mg total THC/serving, package ≤1 oz oil-based liquid, dropper dispensing ≤1 serving, no concentrated water-soluble liquid consumable directly or added to food/beverage.
§1.6 / §7Banned cannabinoids / product typesCorrectedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1482 ; legis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1483(C)(2)Banned for processing/distribution/sale: (i) alcoholic beverage containing any consumable hemp product; (ii) any consumable hemp product for inhalation (LDH shall not approve inhalables, including vapes); (iii) any floral hemp material for retail use; (iv) any product without LDH approval under §1483; (v) product packaged to appeal to children. Processor ban (§1482(C)(2)): no distillate/concentrate containing any derivative of a THC component that is not a naturally occurring cannabinoid. No retailer may add a consumable hemp product to food/beverage sold at retail (§1482(C)(1)). No standalone list of named cannabinoids (e.g. delta-8, THCP) was found in §1482/§1483 — do not assert a named-cannabinoid ban from these sections alone.

§1.6 / §7Consumable hemp testing / labelling; LDH review periodCorrectedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1483(A)(3)–(5),(C),(E),(F),(G)(1)Batch test must show disaggregated THC components by % of total THC, serving size, total THC mg/serving, and solvents, pesticides, microbials, heavy metals; records retained ≥3 years. COA by an independent ISO-accredited (or LDH-approved) laboratory approved by LDH, with no direct/indirect interest in a grower/processor/wholesaler/retailer; University of Louisiana at Monroe lab is the preferred lab once qualified/operational, not exclusive. Label: no medical claims; scannable barcode/QR/web address linked to COA; total THC per serving stated; drug-test-failure warning; contents accurate within 15% variance. §1.6 / §7LDH consumable hemp final rule, January 2026, vs Notice of Intent text (conflict preserved in original)CorrectedLDH — Hemp Final Rule, LR 52:57 (January 2026)RESOLVED in favour of a final rule existing: LDH Hemp Final Rule, Louisiana Register 52:57 (January 2026). Where the original preserved an NOI-vs-final-rule conflict, the final-rule text now governs; any passage quoting only the May 2025 NOI is superseded, not carried as current law. (The LDH Medical Marijuana Final Rule published January 2026 is a separate LDH rule list item; its full LAC citation remains Unverified — see Still Unverified.)
§1.6 / §7Online / shipped consumable hemp salesCorrectedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1484(B) ; legis.la.gov — Act 752, 'remote retailer' definitionRemote retailer = person/entity offering consumable hemp at retail through a digital application, catalog or internet, deliverable directly to a Louisiana consumer. A remote retailer may obtain a retail permit, must meet the same qualifications as in-state retailers, be registered to do business in Louisiana with the Secretary of State, sell only LDH-approved products obtained from a permitted wholesaler, and identify that wholesaler on its website. Each individually registered domain name counts as a place of business; no physical Louisiana place of business is required. In-state processors MAY produce over-limit product ONLY for delivery/transport beyond Louisiana, on a sworn statement that it will leave the state and meets the receiving state's requirements, with 3-year distribution records (§1483(A)(7)). No general 'shipped sales banned/allowed' rule beyond the remote-retailer regime was located in §1484 — do not add one.
§1.6 / §7Gas-station / convenience-store ban (blanket)Correctedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1482(A)(3) ; legis.la.gov — R.S. 3:1484(B)(5)Correct rule is narrower: NO sale at any retail location also authorised to sell gasoline or motor fuel to the ultimate consumer (R.S. 47:712(3)), EXCEPT a facility licensed under R.S. 27:417. Separately, NO new retail permit to an applicant that also holds a Class A (Title 26) alcohol permit; a restaurant/bar holding both a Class A permit and a consumable-hemp retail permit BEFORE 17 June 2024 remains eligible and renewable. A convenience store that does not sell gasoline is not banned by §1482(A)(3) on that ground alone.

§7.2 / §7.3Industrial hemp: 4 LDAF licences $500 each, renewal 30 NovConfirmedLDAF — Hemp Licensing ; LDAF — RegulationsGrower (produce), Processor (non-consumable processing), Handler (transport/harvest/clean/package/test), Seed Producer (produce/transport/sell seed). §2.2Medical sales-tax exemption, state AND local, §47:305.2(B)(11)Confirmedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 47:305.2(B),(B)(11),(C)§305.2(B) heading: exempt from the sales and use tax imposed by 'any taxing authority'; (B)(11) = 'The sale of marijuana recommended for therapeutic use by qualified patients as defined in R.S. 40:1046.' State-and-local exemption therefore stands on the current text. §305.2(C) separately lets a political subdivision provide an exemption for state-exempt items — that does not displace (B)(11)'s 'any taxing authority' wording.
§2.4Consumable hemp excise 3%: statute, payer, fund; 15%/20% proposalsConfirmedlegis.la.gov — R.S. 47:1693 ; LDR Form R-5024 instructionsR.S. 47:1693(A): 3% of retail sales price on each retail sale of consumable hemp products in Louisiana, in addition to state and local sales/use tax, reported monthly by the retailer and paid by the 20th of the following month. Exempt: FDA prescription-approved CBD products and products recommended for therapeutic use under R.S. 40:1046 (§1693(B)). Disposition (§1696): after Bond Security and Redemption Fund requirements, revenues to the Early Childhood Education Fund. The proposed 15% (HB 187) and 20% (HB 235) rates and fund splits are NOT law — see next row.

Federal baseline — given, not re-researched

State-licensed medical marijuana and FDA-approved products moved to Schedule III effective 28 April 2026 (91 FR 22714). All adult-use marijuana remains Schedule I. IRS §280E is generally lifted for Schedule III medical activity only; adult-use remains fully subject to §280E. Hemp: PL 119-37 §781 takes effect 12 November 2026, but PL 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026. After 11 December 2026, the full total-THC hemp definition and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply. USDA enforcement of DEA-registered lab testing for hemp is delayed to 31 December 2026. The federal medical marijuana appropriations rider runs through 11 December 2026. There is no federal cannabis banking law.

Louisiana note applied throughout: Louisiana’s medical programme is state-licensed, so Schedule III / §280E analysis is given for its licensed cultivators (including the former university-affiliated licensees and their contractors, now direct licensees), marijuana pharmacies and labs. Any non-medical possession remains Schedule I federally.

How to read this file — method and limits

Official sources were opened and read directly wherever possible: legis.la.gov, Louisiana Administrative Code / Louisiana Register, LDH, LDAF, the Board of Pharmacy (historic records), ATC, the Department of Revenue, LSU AgCenter and Southern University Agricultural Center, the Governor’s bill actions, and official parish / consolidated-government / city sources. Where a legis.la.gov law page could not be opened in full in the research window, the research notes say so and the passage is cited to the republication actually read (notably Justia’s republication of the Louisiana Laws) and flagged [VERIFY] for a current legis.la.gov re-check before the verbatim text is relied on as current official text. Secondary sources are used only for non-law facts (market figures, polling, events) and are labelled as such, with publication dates. Nothing marked [VERIFY] or [UNAVAILABLE] should be treated as settled. No personal phone numbers or emails of individuals are reproduced. Louisiana has parishes, not counties; “parish” is used throughout.

Cross-part consistency checked across both runs: 2 medical cultivation licences; 10 base marijuana-pharmacy permits (19 satellites listed on the LDH page opened 25 Oct 2026, 29 locations in total); $100,000/year cultivation fee + 7% gross-sales fee; $22,500/year retail fee; consumable hemp 5 mg total THC/serving and 40 mg/package (non-beverage/tincture) under Act 752 of 2024; consumable hemp excise 3%; medical sales-tax exemption for state and local tax; Louisiana runs its own USDA-approved state hemp plan. Where the underlying research tracks flagged a conflict (notably Louisiana §280E decoupling, the LDH retailer-table as-of date, and the LDH January 2026 final rule vs Notice of Intent text), the conflict is preserved in the text and in the gaps lists, not silently resolved. Run 2 resolutions and preserved conflicts are reconciled in the combined research notes at the end of this file.

Scope note. This is part of the combined Louisiana dossier (Parts 0–12), as corrected in the 28 October 2026 audit. See Part 1 (audit) at the top of this file for corrections and items still unverified.

PART 0 — HEADLINES

  1. Medical-only state; no adult-use market. Louisiana has no enacted adult-use legalisation. Only therapeutic (medical) marijuana recommended under La. R.S. 40:1046, and regulated consumable hemp products under La. R.S. Title 3, Part VI, may be sold lawfully. Non-patient possession of ≤14 g is fine-only (see §1.3), but it is NOT legalisation. Sources: R.S. 40:1046(A)(1) and R.S. 40:966(C)(2)(a)(i), quoted in §1.2–1.3; LDH Medical Marijuana page, https://www.ldh.la.gov/bureau-of-sanitarian-services/medical-marijuana (accessed 25 Oct 2026).

  2. Regulation now sits with LDH — two transfers, two dates. - "Per Act 491 and Act 492 of the 2022 Regular Legislature, as of August 1, 2022, the Louisiana Department of Health has assumed regulatory authority over Louisiana's medical (therapeutic) marijuana program." — LDH, https://www.ldh.la.gov/bureau-of-sanitarian-services/medical-marijuana (accessed 25 Oct 2026). - "Act 693 of the 2024 Regular Legislature transferred authority over marijuana retailers from the Louisiana Board of Pharmacy to the Louisiana Department of Health. LDH's Cannabis Program began regulating these retail sites on January 1, 2025." — same LDH page. The LDH page also notes a Potpourri amending the proposed Act 693 rules published 20 January 2025, an Emergency Rule promulgated 28 March 2025, a Notice of Intent published May 2025, and a "Medical Marijuana Final Rule - published January 2026." - What LDAF and the Board of Pharmacy still do is in §1.5. The Board of Pharmacy's historic marijuana-pharmacy rules (La. Admin. Code Title 46, Part LIII, e.g. §2451) are historic after 1 Jan 2025, not current LDH retailer rules — [VERIFY] the current LDH rule citation (LDH refers to a new Subpart; the LDH page does not give a single LAC citation in the text opened).

  3. Universities are OUT as licensees; the two former contractors are IN. Act 150 of 2024 (SB 228, McMath), effective 22 May 2024: "New law removes the universities as the licensees and transfers the licenses on July 1, 2024, to the two contractors who had contracts with the universities on January 1, 2024" and "extends the termination date from January 1, 2025 to July 1, 2030." Source: legis.la.gov Résumé Digest, Act 150 (SB 228) 2024, https://legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1384639 (accessed 25 Oct 2026). LDH confirms: "licenses were transferred to the former permit-holders contracted by the universities in 2024" and names the two current manufacturers as "Advanced Biomedics LLC dba Ilera Holistic Healthcare and Good Day Farm Louisiana LLC" — LDH page above. R.S. 40:1046(H)(1)(b) (2025 text) confirms the 1 July 2024 licences went "to the entities who held contracts with the Louisiana State University Agricultural Center and the Southern University Agricultural Center on January 1, 2024, pursuant to Act No. 261 of the 2015 Regular Session." The two-licence cap remains: "The Louisiana Department of Health shall issue no more than two licenses to cultivate, extract, process, produce, and transport therapeutic marijuana in this state." — R.S. 40:1046(H)(1)(a). LDH research note: R.S. 40:1046(L) still allows LSU AgCenter, Southern University AgCenter and University of Louisiana at Monroe to "conduct research on marijuana for therapeutic use" — research is not a production licence.

  4. Retail cap is 10 base permits, max 30 locations total. LDH lists 10 base permits (one per LDH administrative region as of 1 Aug 2022, with Region 1 holding two base permits — H&W Acquisition and Crescent City Therapeutics — for a total of 10) and 19 satellite locations on the page opened (the statute allows up to 20 satellites; the LDH table shows 19 rows — count the table, do not assume 20 are operating). Statute: "shall limit the number of retail permits granted in the state to no more than ten" and "The total number of marijuana retail locations, including satellite locations… shall not be greater than thirty locations" — R.S. 40:1046(G)(1)(a), (G)(4)(a). Satellite triggers: 3,500 active qualified patients in a region = first satellite; 7,000 = second satellite — R.S. 40:1046(G)(3)(a)–(b), with patient count "conducted and reviewed on a quarterly basis using the preceding twenty-four-month period" — R.S. 40:1046(G)(3)(e) (as amended by Act 150 of 2024). LDH: "No new permits may be issued for non-satellite locations at this time." Annual retail permit fee $22,500 — R.S. 40:1046(G)(1)(b). Cultivation licence fee $100,000/year + $10,000 non-refundable application fee + 7% of gross sales — R.S. 40:1046(H)(4). See Part 2 (other run) for tax/fee distribution; the 7% fee is flagged here only as a headline number.

  5. No state patient card, no state registry for Louisiana residents. LDH: "No state agency maintains a list or directory of clinicians recommending marijuana to patients presently" and "If you are a patient looking for a medical-marijuana recommendation… contact an authorized clinician." The recommendation goes to the chosen retailer; the patient then needs ID at the retailer. Secondary clinic guides agree there is no physical or electronic state card — but that is secondary; the official point is the absence of an LDH patient list/directory and the retailer-based model. Visiting patients ARE different: they must hold another jurisdiction's registry card or equivalent — R.S. 40:1046.1, §1.4.5. Recommendation validity: "Recommendations must bear an expiration date not to exceed 12 months from the date of issuance" — LDH summary of the March 2025 Emergency Rule.

  6. Flower for inhalation is lawful for patients; the only hard statutory purchase cap found is flower. Raw/crude marijuana may be recommended "in any form authorized by the rules and regulations of the Louisiana Department of Health" — R.S. 40:1046(A)(1). Flower was added by Acts 2021, No. 424, effective 1 January 2022 (see §1.2 chronology). Hard cap: "No retailer… shall sell more than two and one-half ounces, or seventy-one grams, of raw or crude marijuana every fourteen days to any individual patient." — R.S. 40:1046(A)(5)(a). LDH repeats: "Patients remain restricted to 71g of marijuana flower per 14-day period." Other dosage forms are limited by the clinician's recommendation, not by a flat statutory gram cap in §1046 — [VERIFY] whether LDH rules impose additional per-form caps; the LDH page does not state one. No home grow: no provision in §1046 authorises patient or caregiver cultivation; all lawful medical marijuana must come through the two licensees and permitted retailers — see §1.3.4.

  7. Physician discretion is the qualifying standard, not a closed list. The statute lists conditions AND a catch-all: "Any condition not otherwise specified in this Subparagraph that an authorized clinician, in his clinical opinion, considers debilitating to an individual patient and is qualified through his clinical education and training to treat." — R.S. 40:1046(A)(2)(a)(xxii). Authorised clinicians are now (i) physicians in good standing with the Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners, (ii) nurse practitioners with prescriptive authority in good standing with the Louisiana State Board of Nursing, and (iii) medical psychologists in good standing with the Board of Medical Examiners — R.S. 40:1046(B). Telehealth recommendations are expressly protected: R.S. 40:1046(K).

  8. Consumable hemp was sharply tightened effective 1 January 2025 (Act 752 of 2024, HB 952). Headline changes, all from R.S. Title 3, Part VI as amended (see §1.6 for verbatim text): - 5 mg total THC per serving (down from 8 mg), 40 mg total THC per package for non-beverage, non-tincture products; beverages: 5 mg per serving, serving ≥12 oz, one serving per tamper-evident container, max 4 containers per package; tinctures: 1 mg per 1 mL serving, max 1 oz oil-based package, dropper dispensing ≤1 serving. - Minimum age 21 for ALL consumable hemp products (was 18, and 21 only for "adult-use" products >0.5 mg/package under the repealed 2022 scheme); age must be verified with a valid federal/state photo ID or digitised ID before the transaction; non-beverage products must be kept inaccessible to the public without employee assistance. - Banned for retail: floral hemp material, any inhalable consumable hemp product (including vapes), any alcoholic beverage containing a consumable hemp product, any product without LDH approval, and any product using a distillate/concentrate containing a derivative of a THC component that is not a naturally occurring cannabinoid. - Location bans: no sale at a retail location also authorised to sell gasoline/motor fuel (qualified truck stops licensed under R.S. 27:417 exempt); and, per the Act 752 digest, no sale on premises holding an alcohol beverage permit unless that entity obtained a hemp permit on or before 17 June 2024 — [VERIFY] this alcohol-premises grandfather clause against the current text of R.S. 3:1484(B)(5), which was not opened in full in this run (see Gaps). - LDH product registration + label approval required; ATC retail/wholesale permits required; 3% consumable hemp excise tax (R.S. 47:1693) remains the enacted rate — 2025 bills to raise it to 15% (HB 187) and 20% (HB 235) did NOT become law in the form proposed (see §1.10).

  9. Small-possession and paraphernalia are fine-only; larger amounts and distribution remain criminal. - ≤14 g, first or subsequent conviction: fine ≤$100, no jail — R.S. 40:966(C)(2)(a)(i), as amended by Act 247 of 2021 (HB 652), effective 1 Aug 2021; summons enforcement; indigency procedure in (a)(ii). - >14 g: 1st — fine ≤$500 and/or ≤6 months parish jail; 2nd — fine ≤$1,000 and/or ≤6 months; 3rd — ≤2 years and fine ≤$2,500; 4th+ — [VERIFY exact text: secondary sources say ≤8 years / ≤$5,000; the FindLaw text opened via search shows (e)(i) for 3rd and the 4th-conviction paragraph was not fully opened — do not publish the 4th tier without re-opening R.S. 40:966(C)(2)(f)]. - Distribution/manufacture (including cultivation): <2.5 lb — 1–10 years, fine ≤$50,000; ≥2.5 lb — 1–20 years at hard labour, fine ≤$50,000 — R.S. 40:966(B)(2). - Marijuana paraphernalia for personal use: 1st $100, 2nd $500, 3rd+ $2,500, no jail — HB 165 of 2024, Act 682 of 2024, signed by the Governor, effective 1 Aug 2024 (legis.la.gov BillInfo and Act 682 digest). - Smoking/vaping in a vehicle on a public highway/right-of-way: $100 fine, secondary enforcement, non-moving violation — R.S. 32:300.4.1, Act 478 of 2022 (HB 234), effective 1 Aug 2022. - Odour: police may not use marijuana odour alone as probable cause to search a home without a warrant — Act 473 of 2022 (HB 629, Bryant), eff. 1 Aug 2022, confirmed on legis.la.gov (enrolled Act 473; Code of Criminal Procedure art. 162.4). The "Act 629 (2024)" label is removed.

  10. 2026 changes to watch (statuses NOT all confirmed on legis.la.gov in this run — see §1.10):

    • SB 270 (2026) — terminally ill patients' use/possession in healthcare facilities (new R.S. 40:1046.5, Act 602 of 2026, eff. 1 Aug 2026). AUDITED 28 Oct 2026 — ENACTED: Act 602 of 2026 (SB 270, Jackson-Andrews), new R.S. 40:1046.5, effective 1 August 2026, became law without the Governor's signature (legis.la.gov BillInfo). The 1 June 2026 date is removed; it is not the legis effective date.
    • HB 568 (2026) — AUDITED 28 Oct 2026 — ENACTED as Act 305 of 2026, signed by the Governor 22 May 2026, effective 1 Aug 2026, amending R.S. 40:981.3(D) and enacting (A)(4) and (E). It applies where a person violates R.S. 40:966–970 while smoking, vaping or otherwise abusing the substance on school property, within 2,000 feet of school property, or on a school bus; the up-to-1-year / up-to-$1,000 cap in new (E) applies only where that act also violates R.S. 40:966(C)(2) (marijuana possession). Other drug-free-zone violations remain under (D) (maximum fine + up to 1.5× longest term). It is not a blanket felony for mere possession at home; MPP is an advocacy source and its "felony for use in your own home within 2,000 feet" framing must not be copied without the statute's "underlying violation" qualifier (see §1.10).
    • HB 373 (2026) — Adult-Use Cannabis Pilot Program (existing medical retailers only, 1 Jan 2027–1 July 2030, proposed 3.5% gross-sales fee) — NOT LAW, no Act number. Legis.la.gov BillInfo as opened in this audit shows only: prefiled 25 Feb 2026, interim calendar 27 Feb 2026, referred to House Health and Welfare 9 Mar 2026, current status "Pending House Health and Welfare". The "voluntarily deferred by sponsor" characterisation was not shown on that legis page and is retained as Unverified in the audit table; it is not stated as a legis action. Adult-use remains NOT law.
    • HB 539 (2026) — consumable hemp location-prohibition repeal (R.S. 3:1484(B)(5)). AUDITED 28 Oct 2026 — NOT LAW: legis.la.gov BillInfo current status is "Withdrawn from the files of the House" 11 May 2026, discharged from Judiciary the same day. It proposed only to repeal the bar on a consumable-hemp retail permit for a Class A on-premises alcohol permittee (pre-17 June 2024 dual holders grandfathered). The bar therefore remains in force.
    • No Louisiana statute, LDH rule, or ATC guidance responding to the federal PL 119-37 / PL 119-103 hemp dates was located in this run — see §1.6.10. That absence is itself a headline: as of 25 Oct 2026, Louisiana's 5 mg / 40 mg regime is still the state law on the books, and it is arithmetically incompatible with a 0.4 mg-per-container federal cap (a single 5 mg beverage is 12.5× the federal cap).

  11. Federal Schedule III / §280E — Louisiana application (given baseline applied, not re-researched). Because Louisiana's programme is state-licensed, its two cultivation licensees (Good Day Farm Louisiana LLC and Advanced Biomedics LLC dba Ilera Holistic Healthcare, as direct LDH licensees since 1 July 2024 — NOT as university contractors), its LDH-permitted marijuana retailers, and its LDH-licensed testing laboratories are the entities within the "state-licensed medical" category described in the baseline, so the general lifting of §280E for Schedule III medical activity applies to their medical activity on the baseline's terms. It does NOT apply to: (a) any adult-use activity (none is lawful in Louisiana in any event); (b) non-medical possession, which remains Schedule I federally; (c) consumable hemp products, which are not marijuana and are not covered by the marijuana rescheduling (their federal future is governed by PL 119-37/119-103, §1.6.10); or (d) any activity outside the state programme (e.g. unlicensed cultivation/distribution). Louisiana state income-tax decoupling from §280E is CONFLICTING in secondary sources and [VERIFY]: one secondary tax guide (Cannabis CPA Tax, 2025 edition) states "Louisiana does not conform to federal IRC §280E" and that medical operators may deduct ordinary expenses on state returns; a CannBus Q3 2026 summary table lists Louisiana §280E conformity as "Not confirmed in available sources." Do NOT publish a decoupling claim as settled until the Louisiana Department of Revenue / R.S. Title 47 conformity provision is located. Note also R.S. 40:1046(J): employers/workers'-comp insurers are NOT obliged to pay for medical marijuana under Title 23 — that provision is unaffected by rescheduling on its face.

  12. Enforcement / compliance headlines with official anchors: Every batch of medical product is tested (LDH page: "Each batch of product is tested for purity and to ensure that it does not exceed the THC-content levels prescribed by the Legislature"); LDH's January 2026 medical rule changed the mold/yeast threshold from 10,000 CFU/g to 100,000 CFU/g and "altered the pesticide testing schedule for marijuana to mirror the one utilized by the state of Oregon" (LDH Emergency Rule summary, March/April 2025 — note the LDH page attributes these changes to the Emergency Rule summary, not necessarily the January 2026 final rule; [VERIFY] which rule text carries each change). Consumable hemp enforcement is permit-based: no permit = no lawful processing/distribution/sale (R.S. 3:1482(A)(1)); unpermitted processing of consumable hemp products carries, under R.S. 3:1483(J), "imprisonment at hard labor for not less than one year nor more than twenty years and… fined not more than fifty thousand dollars" — that is the processor-licence penalty in §1483, distinct from the general Part VI penalty scheme in R.S. 3:1484/1485 history ([VERIFY] current penalty paragraph numbering after Act 752).

PART 1 — LAWS

Audit corrections applied in Part 1 (28 Oct 2026)

Act 286 of 2020 was physician-only discretion; the “authorized clinician” expansion to nurse practitioners with prescriptive authority and medical psychologists came with Act 444 of 2022. Act 424 is Act 424 of 2021 (HB 391), effective 1 January 2022, wherever a secondary summary dated it 2022. Home grow: no standalone ban sentence was found in R.S. 40:1046 — the correct statement is that no home-grow right is created, production is capped at two licences, and sale must be in person by a retail permit holder; unlicensed production/distribution falls under R.S. 40:966(A)–(B). Recommenders are “authorized clinicians” under R.S. 40:1046(B) (physician, nurse practitioner with prescriptive authority, medical psychologist) — the LDH “board-certified physician” phrasing is outdated and is not copied. Caregivers: R.S. 40:966(F)(1) exempts a programme patient, a caregiver as defined in R.S. 15:1503, and a domiciliary parent of a minor; R.S. 40:1046 sets no separate caregiver registration scheme. Visiting patients: Act 438 of 2022, R.S. 40:1046.1.

1.1 Legal status: medical only

Legal for qualified patients, through the state programme only: - A Louisiana authorised clinician's recommendation for a debilitating medical condition, dispensed/sold in person by an LDH-permitted Louisiana retailer, in an LDH-authorised form, within the 71 g / 14-day flower limit and the clinician's recommendation for other forms. See §1.4. - Visiting qualifying patients holding another U.S. jurisdiction's registry card/equivalent, on the §1046.1 procedure. See §1.4.5. - Consumable hemp products that are LDH-registered/label-approved, ATC-permitted, within the §1483 THC/serving/package limits, sold only to persons 21+, at permitted locations. See §1.6. These are hemp products, not marijuana, and buying them does not make a person a medical patient. - Industrial hemp grown/processed/handled under LDAF/USDA authority (Part 7 / Part 5 in other runs for licence detail). Cultivation of industrial hemp outside that authority is itself a Schedule I violation under R.S. 40:966(A)(3) — see §1.2.

NOT legal: - Adult-use / recreational sale, purchase, or possession for non-medical purposes. There is no adult-use licence, no adult-use retail, and no "personal use" quantity that is lawful for a non-patient. The ≤14 g rule is a penalty reduction, not permission: possession remains "unlawful… knowingly or intentionally to possess a controlled dangerous substance classified in Schedule I unless such substance was obtained directly, or pursuant to a valid prescription or order, from a practitioner… or except as otherwise authorized by this Part" — R.S. 40:966(C) (introductory text, via Justia 2022 text). - Home cultivation by patients, caregivers, or any person other than the two LDH licensees — no authorising provision exists in R.S. 40:1046; cultivation by anyone else is manufacture/distribution under R.S. 40:966(A)–(B). See §1.3.4. - Importing marijuana from another state, or exporting Louisiana medical marijuana out of state. R.S. 40:1046(C)(2)(c) requires LDH rules to "provide that no recommended therapeutic marijuana may be sold from, produced from, obtained from, sold to, or transferred to a location outside of this state." LDH retailer summary: "Retailers may not deliver to addresses located outside of the state of Louisiana." - Smoking/vaping marijuana in a vehicle on a public highway/right-of-way (R.S. 32:300.4.1), and — subject to [VERIFY] of the 2026 Act 305 text — covered use on/near school property or on a school bus. - Any consumable hemp product for inhalation, floral hemp at retail, hemp in alcoholic beverages, or any consumable hemp product without LDH approval / ATC permit (R.S. 3:1482). - Federally: any non-medical possession remains Schedule I under the given baseline, even where Louisiana imposes only a $100 fine for ≤14 g. State fine-only treatment does not change federal scheduling.

La. R.S. 40:966 — Penalty for distribution / possession with intent / possession (Schedule I; marijuana, synthetic cannabinoids, heroin) The core criminal statute. §A prohibits manufacture/distribution and non-compliant hemp cultivation; §B sets distribution penalties; §C sets possession penalties; §F gives programme immunity. §A: "it shall be unlawful for any person knowingly or intentionally: (1) To produce, manufacture, distribute or dispense or possess with intent to produce, manufacture, distribute, or dispense, a controlled dangerous substance… classified in Schedule I. … (3) To cultivate, possess, process, or sell industrial hemp, industrial hemp products, or viable industrial hemp seeds not in accordance with the U.S. Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 or the plan submitted by the Department of Agriculture and Forestry that is in compliance with U.S. Department of Agriculture rules." §B(2): marijuana/THC/derivatives/synthetic cannabinoids — "(a) An aggregate weight of less than two and one half pounds, shall be imprisoned, with or without hard labor, for not less than one year nor more than ten years, and pay a fine of not more than fifty thousand dollars. (b) An aggregate weight of two and one half pounds or more, shall be imprisoned at hard labor for not less than one year nor more than twenty years and pay a fine of not more than fifty thousand dollars." §C possession tiers quoted in §1.3. §F(1) immunity quoted in §1.4.6. Amended by Act 247 of 2021 (possession ≤14 g) and later Acts; full Acts line [VERIFY] on legis.la.gov. The 2022 Justia text and the CaseMine "[Effective 1/1/2025]" text agree on the §B(2) weights quoted. https://law.justia.com/codes/louisiana/2022/revised-statutes/title-40/rs-40-966/ ; https://codes.findlaw.com/la/revised-statutes/la-rev-stat-tit-40-sect-966/ (both accessed 25 Oct 2026 via search; legis.la.gov current text to be re-opened)
La. R.S. 40:1001 et seq. — Prescription Monitoring Program (PMP) Requires dispensing reporting. §1046 originally tied dispensing to PMP reporting; §1046.1 (visiting patients) still refers to PMP review/reporting in its 2022 text, while current §1046.1 on legis.la.gov refers to LMMTS. The legis.la.gov §1046.1 text opened defines "LMMTS" as "the electronic seed-to-sale tracking system approved by the department," which suggests a terminology migration that must be confirmed section-by-section.] [VERIFY] legis.la.gov — R.S. 40:1001 et seq.
La. R.S. 40:1046 — Recommendation and sale of marijuana for therapeutic use; production facility licensing; regulations and permitting by LDH (Title 40, Part X-E, Therapeutic Use of Marijuana) THE medical programme statute. Authorises recommendations, defines debilitating conditions + clinician discretion, caps flower sales, creates LMMTS, caps retail permits (10) and cultivation licences (2), sets fees, allows research, sunsets 1 July 2030. A.(1): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Part, any clinician authorized by the provisions of Subsection B of this Section to recommend medical marijuana, referred to in this Section as an 'authorized clinician', may recommend, in any form authorized by the rules and regulations of the Louisiana Department of Health, hereafter referred to as the 'department', raw or crude marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinols, or a chemical derivative of tetrahydrocannabinols for therapeutic use by any patient clinically diagnosed as suffering from a debilitating medical condition." A.(2)(a)(xxii): "Any condition not otherwise specified in this Subparagraph that an authorized clinician, in his clinical opinion, considers debilitating to an individual patient and is qualified through his clinical education and training to treat." A.(5)(a): "No retailer permitted to sell marijuana for therapeutic use in accordance with the provisions of this Section shall sell more than two and one-half ounces, or seventy-one grams, of raw or crude marijuana every fourteen days to any individual patient." E: "Marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinols, or a chemical derivative of tetrahydrocannabinols recommended pursuant to this Section shall be sold in person by a marijuana retail permit holder located in Louisiana." F.(1)(a): LMMTS connectivity "from seed to delivery to an approved laboratory, to wholesale to permitted retailers, to wholesale to another licensed cultivation facility, to delivery to an authorized researcher, to sale to patients or caregivers by permitted retailers, or to destruction." G.(1)(a): 10-permit cap (quoted in Part 0). H.(1)(a): 2-licence cap (quoted in Part 0). H.(4)(c): 7% gross-sales fee, collected by Dept. of Revenue, transferred monthly to Disability Services Fund (R.S. 28:826). I: "The levels of THC in any marijuana produced pursuant to this Section shall be reduced to the lowest acceptable therapeutic levels available through scientifically accepted methods." La. R.S. 40:1046.1 — Sale of marijuana for therapeutic use to visiting qualifying patients Visiting-patient access. Added by Acts 2022, No. 438, §1 (per 2022 Justia text). A.(5): "'Visiting qualifying patient' means a patient with a debilitating medical condition who is not a resident of Louisiana or who has been a resident of Louisiana for less than thirty days and who is in actual possession of a valid medical marijuana registry identification card, or its equivalent, which has been issued under the medical marijuana laws of another state, district, territory, commonwealth, or insular possession of the United States." B: "A visiting qualifying patient may obtain medical marijuana from a marijuana retail permit holder upon producing evidence of his valid medical marijuana registry identification card, or its equivalent…" C.(1): retailer "shall require each visiting qualifying patient to certify on a form approved by the department that the patient has been diagnosed by an authorized clinician with one or more debilitating medical conditions" + name/address/phone + signed non-diversion attestation. Acts 2022, No. 438, §1; later amendments to replace Board of Pharmacy with LDH / PMP with LMMTS [VERIFY exact Act/date — the legis.la.gov text opened uses "department" and "LMMTS," the 2022 Justia text uses "board" and "prescription monitoring program," proving a post-2022 amendment occurred, most plausibly Act 693 of 2024, but the Acts line was not opened]. https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/Law.aspx?d=1295726 ; https://law.justia.com/codes/louisiana/2022/revised-statutes/title-40/rs-40-1046-1/ (accessed 25 Oct 2026)

La. R.S. 40:1021–1025 — Transactions in Drug-Related Objects Prohibited (paraphernalia) Defines drug paraphernalia; prohibits manufacture/delivery/possession etc.; sets the marijuana-paraphernalia personal-use penalty tier. §1021(A): "'drug paraphernalia' means and includes but is not limited to: (1) All equipment, products, and materials of any kind which are used, intended for use, or designed for use in planting, propagating, cultivating, growing, harvesting, manufacturing, compounding, converting, producing, processing, preparing, testing, analyzing, packaging, repackaging, storing, containing, concealing, injecting, ingesting, inhaling, or otherwise introducing into the human body a controlled substance in violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law, as scheduled in R.S. 40:964." Marijuana-paraphernalia personal-use penalties (HB 165 enrolled text): "(1) On a first conviction, a fine of one hundred dollars. (2) On a second conviction, a fine of five hundred dollars. (3) On a third or subsequent conviction, a fine of two thousand five hundred dollars." — for "quantities of paraphernalia not exceeding those required for individual personal use" for paraphernalia "intended for, or used solely for, the inhalation, ingestion, epidermal or sublingual absorption, or other method of introducing marijuana or marijuana derivatives into the human body." HB 165 (2024), Act 682 of 2024, eff. 1 Aug 2024 (legis.la.gov). Pre-2024 penalties were up to $300 / 15 days (1st), $500 / 6 months (2nd), $2,500 / up to 2 years hard labour (subsequent) per NORML summary — historical only. https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/Law.aspx?d=96972 (§1021) ; https://legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1379657 (HB 165 enrolled) ; http://norml.org/blog/2024/06/24/louisiana-governor-signs-legislation-decriminalizing-possession-of-marijuana-paraphernalia/ (accessed 25 Oct 2026)

1.3 Penalties, cultivation, paraphernalia, consumption, smoking, product forms

1.3.1 Possession by non-patients (R.S. 40:966(C)(2)) — table: | Amount / conviction | Penalty (verbatim / paraphrase as labelled) | |—|—| | ≤14 g, first OR any subsequent conviction — verbatim: "On a first conviction or any subsequent conviction, wherein the offender possesses fourteen grams or less, the offender shall be fined not more than one hundred dollars." — §966(C)(2)(a)(i) | Fine ≤$100 only. No imprisonment. Summons enforcement (Act 247 digest). Indigency: if the offender "alleges indigency, or otherwise fails to pay," the court "shall determine whether the defendant has willfully refused to pay or has made bona fide efforts to legally acquire resources to pay" and, if not wilful + bona fide efforts, "shall use its discretion to alternatives, including installment payments or community service" — §966(C)(2)(a)(ii). | | >14 g, 1st conviction — verbatim: "the offender shall be fined not more than five hundred dollars, imprisoned in the parish jail for not more than six months, or both." — §966(C)(2)(b) | Fine ≤$500 and/or ≤6 months parish jail. | | >14 g, 2nd conviction — verbatim (via FindLaw text): fine ≤$1,000, parish jail ≤6 months, or both — §966(C)(2)(d) | Fine ≤$1,000 and/or ≤6 months. | | >14 g, 3rd conviction — verbatim (via FindLaw text): "shall be sentenced to imprisonment, with or without hard labor, for not more than two years, shall be fined not more than two thousand five hundred dollars." — §966(C)(2)(e)(i); probation, if granted, requires a court-approved substance-abuse programme + four 8-hour days of community service — (e)(ii) | ≤2 years + fine ≤$2,500. | | >14 g, 4th or subsequent conviction | [VERIFY — secondary sources (NORML; LegalClarity) state ≤8 years + fine ≤$5,000 under §966(C)(2)(f)(i); the paragraph was not opened verbatim in this run. Do not publish until opened.] | | Predicate-conviction washout | §966(C)(2)(c): a person sentenced under (a) or (b) who has no further marijuana-possession conviction for 2 years from completion of sentence/probation/parole/suspension "shall not have the conviction used as a predicate conviction for enhancement purposes," occurring only once per person. | | Distribution / possession with intent / manufacture (incl. cultivation) | <2.5 lb: 1–10 years (with or without hard labour) + fine ≤$50,000; ≥2.5 lb: 1–20 years at hard labour + fine ≤$50,000 — §966(B)(2). Second/subsequent doubling: [VERIFY — NORML states the term/fine authorised is doubled; the doubling provision (§966(B) / §982) was not opened verbatim.] Distribution by a person >25 to a minor, and distribution to a minor ≥3 years junior: [VERIFY — NORML cites R.S. 40:981/982 with 10–30 years / 5–30 years; not opened verbatim.] |

Change history for the 14 g threshold: Before Act 247 of 2021, first-conviction ≤14 g carried a fine up to $300, imprisonment up to 15 days, or both, with enhanced penalties for subsequent convictions — Act 247 Résumé Digest (HB 652, Glover), https://legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1236895 (accessed 25 Oct 2026). Act 247, effective 1 Aug 2021, replaced that with the flat ≤$100 fine for first or subsequent ≤14 g convictions and retained the >14 g scheme. It did NOT decriminalise in the sense of making possession lawful, and it did NOT change distribution penalties.

1.3.2 Home grow — prohibited. Confirmed by absence + structure: R.S. 40:1046 authorises only two LDH cultivation licences and LDH-permitted retail sale; it contains no patient/caregiver cultivation authorisation, no plant-count provision, and no home-grow registration. Cultivation by any other person is "produce, manufacture" under R.S. 40:966(A)(1) and punishable under §966(B)(2) above. Secondary sources uniformly state "No Home Cultivation Permitted" / "All medical cannabis must come from a licensed pharmacy" — consistent with the statute, but the statutory point is the absence of authorisation, which the parent should state as such rather than citing a non-existent "home grow ban" section.

1.3.3 Paraphernalia. Definition §1021(A)(1) quoted in §1.2. Possession for personal marijuana use: fines only ($100 / $500 / $2,500) after HB 165 (2024), eff. 1 Aug 2024. Other paraphernalia offences (manufacture/delivery, delivery to minors, advertising — R.S. 40:1023–1025) were NOT opened in this run: [VERIFY] whether the HB 165 fine-only tier applies only to the personal-use possession paragraph or more broadly, and what penalties remain for sale/delivery of paraphernalia. Do not state that "paraphernalia is decriminalised" without that qualifier. Note: devices used solely for inhaling medical marijuana by a programme patient in an allowed form are described in secondary sources as excluded from the definition — [VERIFY] against current §1021, as the §1021 text opened does not show that exclusion in the portion read.

1.3.4 Public consumption and smoking rules. - Vehicle: banned, $100, secondary enforcement, non-moving — R.S. 32:300.4.1 (§1.2). - General public consumption / smoking in public places: NO general public-consumption statute was located in this run. Do NOT invent a public-smoking ban or a "private use only" rule from other states. What exists is: (a) the vehicle ban; (b) the programme's in-person retail sale + no out-of-state delivery rules; (c) the reported 2026 school-zone enhancement (see §1.10, [VERIFY]); (d) smoke-free-air / local ordinance rules, which belong in Part 3 (other run) and were not researched here. - Patient smoking: raw/crude flower for inhalation IS an authorised form (Act 424, eff. 1 Jan 2022). The earlier "except for inhalation" limitation and the metered-dose-inhaler proviso are historical. Metered-dose inhaler authorisation remains in §1046(A)(7): "Nothing in this Subsection shall be construed to prevent the department from authorizing, by rule, medical marijuana in a form to be administered by metered-dose inhaler."

1.4 Medical programme

1.4.1 Qualification — physician/clinician discretion beyond the list. The list in §1046(A)(2)(a) is: cancer; glaucoma; Alzheimer's, ALS, Huntington's, Lewy body dementia, motor neuron disease, Parkinson's, spinal muscular atrophy; HIV-positive status; AIDS; cachexia/wasting; seizure disorders; epilepsy; spasticity; severe muscle spasms; intractable pain (defined in (A)(2)(c) as pain whose cause cannot be removed/treated with consent and for which, in generally accepted practice, no relief/cure is possible or none found after reasonable efforts, "so chronic and severe as to otherwise warrant an opiate prescription"); Crohn's; muscular dystrophy; multiple sclerosis; PTSD; specified autism-spectrum-associated conditions; traumatic brain injury; concussion diagnosed by an authorised clinician; chronic pain associated with fibromyalgia; chronic pain associated with sickle cell disease; any condition for which the patient is receiving hospice/palliative care; AND the catch-all (A)(2)(a)(xxii) quoted in Part 0. Autism-spectrum conditions for patients under 18 require compliance with §1046 and consultation with a pediatric subspecialist — §1046(A)(2)(b). "Recommend" means "an opinion of any authorized clinician, provided within a bona fide clinician-patient relationship, that, in the sincere judgment of the clinician, therapeutic cannabis may be helpful to the patient's condition or symptoms and is communicated by any means allowed by the department" — §1046(A)(3). "Any authorized clinician may recommend medical marijuana to any patient suffering from a debilitating medical condition with whom he shares a bona fide clinician-patient relationship." — §1046(A)(4). Telehealth: §1046(K) (quoted in §1.2 table). Adverse events/health outcomes must be reported by authorised clinicians "to the data system provided for in R.S. 40:1168.1 et seq." — §1046(A)(6) ([VERIFY] what that data system is in practice — PMP vs LMMTS vs a separate outcomes registry).

1.4.2 Who may recommend. §1046(B) (quoted in Part 0): (1) physicians licensed by and in good standing with the Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners; (2) nurse practitioners licensed by and in good standing with the Louisiana State Board of Nursing "who has prescriptive authority conferred by" that Board; (3) medical psychologists licensed by and in good standing with the Board of Medical Examiners. LDH page: "Any authorized clinician as defined in La. R.S. 40:1046 who is in good standing with the relevant governing board, may issue marijuana recommendations" and "The Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners (LSBME) no longer tracks or monitors authorized clinicians specifically for the purpose of overseeing the activity of issuing recommendations." Note the §1046(B) text opened still says "licensed physician" in §49:1016 (2022) — that employment statute has not been updated to the broader "authorised clinician" language; do not "correct" it in quotation.

1.4.3 Registry / card — NO state card or registry for residents. See Part 0, item 5. The mechanism is: clinician → recommendation transmitted to the patient's chosen retailer (LDH page: patient should "contact an authorized clinician"; retailer table is the patient-facing directory) → retailer verifies in LMMTS before sale (§1046(F)(1)(a): seller "shall review the patient's information in the database of the LMMTS prior to the selling thereof") → patient presents ID. Recommendation contents (secondary synthesis of LDH rules — [VERIFY] against current LAC Title 51, Part XXIX): clinician name/address/phone; patient name/address/DOB; qualifying condition; contraindicated dosage forms; date; expiration ≤12 months. There is no state application fee for patients in the statute opened. Whether a retailer charges its own dispensing/consultation fee is a commercial fact, not in the statute — [VERIFY] / do not state.

1.4.4 Purchase limits. Flower: 71 g / 14 days (§1046(A)(5)(a)). Other forms: "any amount… in excess of the authorized clinician's recommendation" must be refused — secondary synthesis of LDH rules (Flourish state page, accessed via search 25 Oct 2026); the statute itself does not state a gram cap for non-flower forms. Retailer must cross-reference LMMTS sales history before every sale (§1046(F)). No daily limit, no 30-day supply cap, and no possession cap for patients (as distinct from the purchase cap) was found in §1046 — [VERIFY] whether LDH rules impose a possession limit; do not import another state's 30-day rule. Note: some secondary guides describe "daily-dosage and 30-day-supply rules" — that description was NOT verified against LDH rules in this run and must not be repeated as law.

1.4.5 Caregivers. Statute: §1046(F)(1)(a) contemplates "sale to patients or caregivers by permitted retailers," and historic Board rule §2451 (LAC Title 46, Part LIII) provided that a marijuana pharmacy "may dispense and sell marijuana to a patient with a recommendation… or the patient's caregiver" and that "only a pharmacist, pharmacy intern, or pharmacy technician may sell marijuana to patients and caregivers" (sale of dispensed product by any pharmacy employee). The §966(F)(1) immunity expressly covers "a caregiver as defined in R.S. 15:1503" and "any person who is a domiciliary parent of a minor child who possesses medical marijuana on behalf of his minor child." What §1046/§15:1503 require for caregiver designation (age, residency, background check, patient limit, separate registration) was NOT opened in this run: secondary guides claim no separate state caregiver card, parents/guardians for minors, and (in one guide) 21+ / Louisiana resident / background check / ≤2 patients — ALL [VERIFY] against R.S. 15:1503 and current LDH rules before publication. Do not publish the secondary caregiver eligibility list as law.

1.4.6 Visiting / out-of-state patients. R.S. 40:1046.1 (quoted in §1.2): non-resident OR resident <30 days + valid registry card/equivalent from another U.S. state/district/territory/commonwealth/insular possession + debilitating condition + department-approved certification form (name/address/phone + signed non-diversion attestation) + retailer retention of (i) registry card/equivalent, (ii) valid driver's licence or other government photo ID, (iii) signed form. 2022 text additionally required the dispensing pharmacist to review PMP records, consult the patient's physician on concerns, report the transaction to PMP, perform prospective drug-utilisation review, and counsel every time, and to refuse if the card was revoked/expired/invalid, fraudulently obtained, application/certifications falsified, or the patient knowingly violated Louisiana medical marijuana law — [VERIFY] whether those pharmacist duties survive in the current LDH/LMMTS version of §1046.1 (the legis.la.gov text opened shows only Subsections A–C(1) in the portion read). Visiting patients are also covered by §966(F)(1) immunity (quoted below). There is NO reciprocity obligation in the other direction: Louisiana recommendations do not entitle the holder to buy in another state, and transporting marijuana across state lines remains federally unlawful (given baseline + §1046(C)(2)(c) no-out-of-state-transfer rule).

1.4.7 Immunity (verbatim). R.S. 40:966(F)(1): "Any person who is a patient of the state-sponsored medical marijuana program in Louisiana, and possesses medical marijuana in a form permissible under R.S. 40:1046 for a condition enumerated therein, a caregiver as defined in R.S. 15:1503, any person who is a domiciliary parent of a minor child who possesses medical marijuana on behalf of his minor child in a form permissible under R.S. 40:1046 for a condition enumerated therein pursuant to a legitimate medical marijuana prescription or recommendation issued by a licensed health professional authorized by R.S. 40:1046(B) to recommend medical marijuana to patients, or any visiting qualifying patient as defined in R.S. 40:1046.1 shall be exempt from the provisions of this Section. This Paragraph shall not prevent the arrest or prosecution of any person for diversion of marijuana or any of its derivatives or other conduct outside the scope of the state-sponsored medical marijuana program." R.S. 40:966(F)(2) (current LDH wording via CaseMine): retailers and their employees/board members/directors/agents are exempt for possession at an LDH-rule-designated location or distribution in an LDH-approved form to a patient with a valid recommendation, subject to the same diversion / LDH-rule-violation carve-out. Note the immunity text still says "for a condition enumerated therein" — its interaction with the (A)(2)(a)(xxii) catch-all (a condition "not otherwise specified") is a textual tension to flag, not resolve by paraphrase: [VERIFY] whether any Act updated §966(F) to track the catch-all.

Publishes retailer/base + satellite tables, lab list, final/emergency rules. Act 491 + Act 492 of 2022 (production/labs/fees, eff. 1 Aug 2022, with Act 492 eff. 16 June 2022 for its fee provisions per §1046 Acts line — [VERIFY] split effective dates); Act 693 of 2024 (retailers, eff. 1 Jan 2025); LDH page, https://www.ldh.la.gov/bureau-of-sanitarian-services/medical-marijuana
