Federal baseline (given, NOT re-researched in this run): State-licensed medical marijuana and FDA-approved products moved to Schedule III effective 28 April 2026 (91 FR 22714); adult-use marijuana remains Schedule I; IRS §280E is generally lifted for Schedule III medical activity only; hemp: PL 119-37 §781 takes effect 12 November 2026, but PL 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026, after which the full total-THC hemp definition and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply; USDA DEA-registered-lab hemp testing enforcement is delayed to 31 December 2026; the federal medical marijuana appropriations rider runs through 11 December 2026; there is no federal cannabis banking law. Nothing found in this run contradicts that baseline. No new Louisiana agency response to the 12 November / 11 December 2026 federal hemp dates was located in this run's searches; Run 1's [UNAVAILABLE] on that point is therefore carried forward, not resolved — see §7.9.

§0 — Run 1 anchors carried forward unchanged

These Run 1 facts are the baseline for Parts 7–8. They are repeated here only so this file can be read on its own; they were not re-decided in this run.

  • Louisiana is medical only; no adult-use law is enacted. Sources: Run 1 Parts 0–1, citing La. R.S. 40:1046 and LDH Medical Marijuana page, https://www.ldh.la.gov/bureau-of-sanitarian-services/medical-marijuana (accessed 25 Oct 2026 in Run 1).
  • LDH regulates medical marijuana: production/labs transferred by Acts 491/492 of 2022 (effective 1 August 2022); retailers transferred from the Board of Pharmacy by Act 693 of 2024 (effective 1 January 2025). Source: Run 1 Part 1 §1.5 / Part 4 §4.2.2, LDH page https://ldh.la.gov/page/medical-marijuana (accessed 25 Oct 2026).
  • Act 150 of 2024 (SB 228) transferred the 2 medical cultivation licences on 1 July 2024 to the former university contractors — now Good Day Farm Louisiana LLC and Advanced Biomedics LLC d/b/a Ilera Holistic Healthcare — and the programme sunset is 1 July 2030. Source: Run 1 Part 4 §4.1.2, citing R.S. 40:1046(H) and the LDH page.
  • 10 base marijuana-pharmacy (retail) permits + 19 satellites listed = 29 locations on the LDH page as counted 25 October 2026; $22,500/year retail fee per permit holder; $100,000/year cultivation fee + 7% gross-sales fee. Source: Run 1 Part 4 §§4.2.3–4.2.4, citing R.S. 40:1046(G)(1)(b) and (H)(4) and https://ldh.la.gov/page/medical-marijuana (accessed 25 Oct 2026).
  • No patient card/registry; clinician-discretion qualification; flower 71 g / 14 days; no home grow; ≤14 g for non-patients is fine-only up to $100 (Act 247 of 2021). Source: Run 1 Part 1 §§1.3–1.4.
  • Consumable hemp, Act 752 of 2024 (HB 952), effective 1 January 2025: 5 mg total THC per serving, 40 mg per package (non-beverage/tincture); beverages 5 mg in ≥12 oz, max 4 containers per package; tinctures 1 mg/mL, max 1 oz; age 21+; LDH product registration + ATC permits; gas-station retail ban (qualified truck-stop exemption). Source: Run 1 Part 1 §1.6 and Part 4 §4.4, citing R.S. 3:1481–1484 and the Act 752 enrolled text, https://legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1382781 (accessed 25 Oct 2026 in Run 1).
  • Medical marijuana is exempt from state AND local sales tax (R.S. 47:305.2(B)(11)); consumable hemp excise tax is 3%. Source: Run 1 Part 2 §§2.2, 2.4.
  • A hemp licence is NOT a medical marijuana licence, and a medical licence is NOT a hemp licence. The two supply chains are regulated by different statutes (R.S. 3:1461 et seq. and R.S. 3:1481 et seq. for hemp; R.S. 40:1046 for therapeutic marijuana) and, for consumable hemp, by different agencies for different steps (see §7.1). No provision located in this run authorises a hemp licensee to grow, process, or sell therapeutic marijuana, or a therapeutic marijuana licensee to sell consumable hemp without the hemp authorisations for that activity.

PART 7 — HEMP LICENCES

Audit corrections applied in Part 7 (28 Oct 2026)

Act 752 (HB 952) 2024: §1 effective 1 Jan 2025; §3 (Class A provision) effective 19 June 2024 — do not date the whole Act to June 2024. Total THC (R.S. 3:1481) is any combination of THC, THCA, a THC component, or any derivative; a THC component is a naturally occurring cannabinoid component of hemp. The 5 mg / 40 mg limits apply to products other than beverages and tinctures; nonedible products are not subject to those serving/package limits (R.S. 3:1483(B)(6)(d)). Beverage: a serving shall not exceed 5 mg total THC and shall not be less than 12 ounces, in an individual tamper-evident container, package ≤4 containers. Tincture: 1 mL serving, ≤1 mg total THC, package ≤1 oz oil-based liquid, dropper dispensing ≤1 serving. Banned: an alcoholic beverage containing a consumable hemp product; any inhalable product (including vapes, which LDH shall not approve); floral hemp for retail sale; any unapproved product; packaging appealing to children; a processor distillate/concentrate containing a derivative of a THC component that is not naturally occurring; a retailer adding a consumable hemp product to food/beverage sold at retail. No named-cannabinoid ban (e.g. delta-8, THCP) is asserted from R.S. 3:1482/1483 alone. Age 21+: 2025 Act 233 (HB 12), eff. 1 Aug 2025, added R.S. 14:93.16 (sale/distribution/delivery to a person under 21: $500–$1,000 fine and/or 30 days–6 months) and R.S. 14:93.17 (under-21 purchase/possession: fine ≤$100, citation, not on criminal history). LDH product review is 60 business days (R.S. 3:1483(G)(1)); a permitted wholesaler/retailer may sell from the day after the 60th business day if LDH has not notified deficiencies — an LDH FAQ showing 15 days is outdated against the current statute. The University of Louisiana at Monroe laboratory is the preferred consumable-hemp lab once qualified/operational, not exclusive. Remote retailers: digital/catalog/internet sale deliverable directly to a Louisiana consumer, SOS-registered, selling only LDH-approved products from a permitted wholesaler identified on its website; each domain name counts as a place of business; no physical Louisiana place of business is required. Gas-station rule: see Part 1 correction — no sale at a location also authorised to sell gasoline/motor fuel to the ultimate consumer (R.S. 47:712(3)), except a facility licensed under R.S. 27:417. LDAF industrial hemp: 4 licences $500 each, renewals due 30 November; background-check cadence remains Unverified (current R.S. 3:1465 not opened; 2020 text said initial or annual renewal, secondary summaries say initial + every 3 years).

7.0 At a glance — every Louisiana hemp licence/permit type

Louisiana does not have one hemp licence. It has a three-agency split, and a business that grows hemp, turns it into a consumable product, and sells it at retail needs up to three different authorisations — one per activity — plus a per-product registration for each consumable product. The table below is the complete inventory found in this run. "Other" types that were searched for and not found as current, standalone types are listed separately in §7.8 so the absence is auditable.

What one licence does NOT cover: An LDAF grower licence does not authorise processing into a consumable product (that is LDH), and neither LDAF nor LDH authorises retail sale (that is ATC). A retailer permit does not authorise growing or processing. A product registration does not by itself authorise a person to process — the product must be submitted through a permitted processor (in-state or out-of-state) since Act 752 (see §7.6). Source for the three-agency split: LDAF regulations page, https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp/regulations (opened 25 Oct 2026): "LDAF regulates the production, handling, and processing of non-consumable hemp products. Medical marijuana production and the processing of consumable hemp products are regulated by the Louisiana Department of Health" and "Businesses or individuals interested in selling CBD products must also be registered through the Louisiana Office of Alcohol and Tobacco Control."

7.1 USDA-approved state plan — Louisiana runs its own plan, not USDA direct licensing

Answer in one line: Louisiana runs its own USDA-approved state plan. It does not use the USDA direct producer-licence programme while that plan is in effect. A Louisiana grower therefore applies to LDAF, not to USDA, for a production licence.

  • Current AMS status (opened directly): USDA Agricultural Marketing Service, "List of USDA-approved Hemp Plans," updated 17 February 2026, lists: "| Louisiana | LA Approved Plan (pdf)* |" — https://www.ams.usda.gov/rules-regulations/hemp/state-and-tribal-plan-review (opened 25 Oct 2026). The page's descriptors state: "Approved *: Plan approved under the final rule which took effect March 22, 2021" and "USDA Hemp Producer License: USDA will issue the producer license" (the latter is the status for states without an approved plan, e.g. Mississippi, New Hampshire, and Iowa on the same page — not Louisiana).
  • Original approval — date discrepancy carried from Run 1, with a reconciliation: LSU AgCenter Staff Report No. 2020-53 (September 2020) states: "On December 23, 2019, Louisiana's state industrial hemp plan was approved by the USDA" and "As of December 27, 2019, the LDAF Industrial Hemp Program began accepting license applications" — https://www.lsuagcenter.com/articles/page1605805806025 (accessed 25 Oct 2026). USDA's own public announcement is dated 27 December 2019: "USDA Approves First State and Tribal Hemp Production Plans … The plans were submitted by the states of Louisiana, New Jersey, and Ohio" — https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDAAMS/bulletins/27296bc?reqfrom=share (accessed 25 Oct 2026). Reconciliation (not a Run 1 overwrite): 23 December is the date LSU reports as the approval date; 27 December is the date of USDA's public announcement and the date LDAF began accepting applications. Whether the formal USDA approval letter is dated 23 or 27 December 2019 is [VERIFY — obtain the USDA approval letter / AMS plan PDF for Louisiana from the AMS page linked above]. Run 1 recorded the same 23 vs 27 December tension; this run does not resolve it.
  • Applications opened: LDAF's own regulations page states: "LDAF began the hemp licensing application process in early February 2020" — https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp/regulations (opened 25 Oct 2026). That sits alongside LSU's "27 December 2019" application-open date above; the difference is most plausibly announcement/acceptance vs the first full application round, but the exact sequence is [VERIFY against LDAF's 2019–2020 programme announcements] and is not asserted as a single date here.
  • Enabling state law: LDAF's regulations page states: "Act 164 of the 2019 Louisiana Legislative Session, now known as the Industrial Hemp Law, was signed by Governor John Bel Edwards on June 6, 2019, which recognized industrial hemp as an agricultural commodity in Louisiana. The Law authorizes the commercial cultivation and processing of hemp in Louisiana. The Law also requires the LDAF to license and regulate hemp in Louisiana." — same LDAF regulations page (opened 25 Oct 2026). The Industrial Hemp Law is R.S. 3:1461 et seq. (see §7.2).
  • What "own plan" means in practice: Under R.S. 3:1483(B)(1) (legis.la.gov, opened 25 Oct 2026), a consumable hemp product for Louisiana use must "Be produced from hemp grown by a licensee authorized to grow hemp by the United States Department of Agriculture or under an approved state plan pursuant to the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018, P.L. 115-334, or under an authorized state pilot program pursuant to the Agriculture Act of 2014, P.L. 113-79." Louisiana-grown hemp therefore qualifies through the Louisiana state plan, and hemp grown under another approved state plan or a USDA licence also qualifies on the face of that paragraph — the product still needs Louisiana LDH registration and an ATC-permitted seller (see §§7.5–7.11).
  • USDA direct licensing — when it would apply: Only if Louisiana's plan were withdrawn by the state or revoked by USDA. The AMS page states an approved plan "remains in effect unless withdrawn by the State or Tribal government or revoked by USDA pursuant to the procedures described in the Final Rule" — same AMS page (opened 25 Oct 2026). No withdrawal or revocation of Louisiana's plan was located in this run. Consistent with Run 1 Part 5 §5.9, no Louisiana USDA-direct licensee list was located, and none would be expected while the state plan is in effect.
  • Federal hemp-definition dates and the state plan: The given federal baseline (PL 119-37 §781 / PL 119-103 §2019, 12 November / 11 December 2026) changes the federal definition of hemp and the per-container cap; it does not, on its face, revoke Louisiana's USDA-approved production plan. Whether USDA/AMS will require Louisiana to re-submit or amend its plan to reflect a total-THC definition or a per-container cap is [UNAVAILABLE — no USDA/AMS Louisiana-specific re-submission notice was located in this run]. See also §7.9 on the Louisiana product side.

7.2 The industrial hemp statute — R.S. 3:1461 et seq. (LDAF licences)

Statute: Industrial Hemp Law, R.S. 3:1461 et seq., enacted by Act 164 of 2019 (signed 6 June 2019, per LDAF regulations page above); amended by Acts 2020, No. 344; Acts 2021, No. 336; Acts 2022, No. 498 (effective 16 June 2022) — history line as shown on the current R.S. 3:1465 page on legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/LawPrint.aspx?d=1147977 (opened 25 Oct 2026). The same page gives the Act 462 of 2022 cross-reference on the LDAF regulations page (see §7.2 note below).

Definitions (LDAF regulations page, opened 25 Oct 2026):

"By law, industrial hemp includes all plant parts and varieties of the cannabis plant and any part of the plant cultivated or possessed by an industrial hemp licensee, with a total THC concentration level of not more than 0.3% on a dry weight basis." "Non-consumable industrial hemp is any product derived from industrial hemp that does not contain any cannabinoid, including cannabidiol, and is not intended for consumption or topical use." "Consumable hemp product means any product derived from industrial hemp that contains any cannabinoid, including cannabidiol, and is intended for consumption or topical use. This shall include commercial feed, pet products, and hemp floral material."

THC measurement (LDAF regulations page, opened 25 Oct 2026): "The federally defined limit for THC is no more than 0.3% Total THC. In Louisiana, LDAF samples and tests industrial hemp to evaluate Total THC concentration levels prior to harvest. THC is measured post-decarboxylation, which is the conversion of delta-9 THC-a into delta-9 THC with heat. This is commonly referred to as Total THC. The values for THC and THCa (adjusted for molecular weight conversion) are added together. Final answers are subject to a further adjustment for uncertainty … The uncertainty value used in Louisiana is 0.104%." And: "If hemp has more than 0.3% of THC, it is considered marijuana and is not in compliance. This will result in LDAF issuing a stop order. Anything testing over 1.0% THC will result in LDAF taking further regulatory action."

Licensure — R.S. 3:1465 (verbatim, legis.la.gov, opened 25 Oct 2026):

"A.(1)(a) Each seed producer shall obtain an annual license issued by the department. The license shall authorize the licensee to produce, transport, and sell approved seeds to licensed industrial hemp growers, seed producers, handlers, and processors." "(2) A grower of industrial hemp shall obtain an annual license issued by the department. The license shall authorize the licensee to possess, store, cultivate, trim, dry, cure, and transport industrial hemp in this state." "(3) A processor of industrial hemp shall obtain an annual license issued by the department. The license shall authorize the licensee to possess, store, process, and transport industrial hemp in this state." "(4) A handler of industrial hemp shall obtain an annual license issued by the department. The license shall authorize the licensee to handle industrial hemp in this state." "B. Any person desiring to obtain a license shall apply to the commissioner for a license on a form prescribed by the commissioner. A license must be obtained before a person purchases or obtains any industrial hemp seeds." "C.(1) The application for any grower, processor, handler, or seed producer license shall include the following information: (a) The name and address of the applicant. (b) The name and address of the designated responsible party, if the applicant is a business entity. (c) If applicable, the legal description and global positioning coordinates of the land area to be used to produce or process industrial hemp. (2) If any changes are made to the required information in Paragraph (1) of this Subsection, the applicant shall resubmit the application to the department within fifteen days." "D.(1) Upon application for initial licensure and every three years thereafter, each applicant shall be required to submit to a criminal background check pursuant to the provisions of this Subsection. For purposes of this Subsection, 'applicant' shall mean an applicant or designated responsible party as defined in R.S. 3:1462." "D.(5) No person shall be eligible to obtain a license if convicted under state or federal law of any of the following: (a) A felony within the ten years immediately preceding the date of application. (b) A drug-related misdemeanor within the two years immediately preceding the date of application." "E. The applicant is responsible for any employee working under the applicant's license." "F. The provisions of this Section shall not apply to the Louisiana State University Agricultural Center, the Southern University Agricultural Center, the University of Louisiana at Monroe Agribusiness Program, and the University of Louisiana at Monroe College of Pharmacy when performing research and development as provided for in R.S. 3:1469."

Run 1 clarification — background-check frequency (NOT a silent change): Run 1 Part 4 §4.1.3 summarised the LDAF page's "complete your background check" step and the 60-day rule for multiple licences, without stating a frequency. The current R.S. 3:1465(D)(1) text opened in this run says "upon application for initial licensure and every three years thereafter." That three-year cycle is the Act 498 of 2022 change: the Act 498 résumé digest (legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1292582, accessed 25 Oct 2026) states: "Prior law required a criminal background check upon application for initial licensure or annual license renewal for growers, seed producers, processors, and handlers. New law changes the criminal background check requirement to upon application for initial licensure and every three years thereafter." The LDAF page's 60-day rule is separate and still applies: "If applying for multiple licenses, you're only required to provide one state and federal background check report as long as the background check is performed within 60 days of the date the application is received by LDAF" — https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp/hemp-licensing (opened 25 Oct 2026). LAC 7:XIII §1315(D) adds: "LDAF shall not accept a criminal background check report that was issued more than 60 days prior to submission of the application" (LAC March 2026 compilation, opened 25 Oct 2026 — see §7.3).

Fees — LDAF licences (LAC, opened directly): LAC Title 7, Part XIII, Chapter 13, §1317 (March 2026 compilation, https://assets.ctfassets.net/pc5e1rlgfrov/10zor8iRixgMZBQkgq4jXJ/6ce3e37737e9d0cf9171f74582a1e575/Seed-Rules-Regulations_title7_Seed_XIII_Rev_03_2026.pdf, opened 25 Oct 2026):

"A. License Fees — 1. The annual fee for a seed producer, grower, processor, and handler license shall be $500 each. 2. New license fees are due upon notification of application approval. No license shall be issued until payment of the license fee is received by LDAF." "B. Sample Testing Fees — 1. THC testing of industrial hemp plant parts shall be $250 per sample. 2. THC testing fees are due at the time of sample collection."

That matches the LDAF licensing page exactly: "Licenses cost $500 each, and renewals are due by November 30 of each year" — https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp/hemp-licensing (opened 25 Oct 2026). Fee-cap note: The 2020 engrossed HB 843 text (legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1170307, accessed 25 Oct 2026) states for R.S. 3:1467: "The combined total of the annual application fee and license fee shall not exceed five hundred dollars, and the testing fee shall not exceed two hundred fifty dollars." The current R.S. 3:1467 text was not opened in this run, so that cap is cited to the 2020 engrossed text and marked [VERIFY — open current R.S. 3:1467 on legis.la.gov]. The $500-per-licence practice on the LDAF page and in LAC §1317 is consistent with the cap, but the cap itself is not asserted here as current text without that check.

PROPOSED fee change — do NOT use as law: SB 495 (2024, original text, legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1361511, accessed 25 Oct 2026) proposed in §1467(B): "(1) Seed producer fee - $500.00. (2) Grower of industrial hemp fee - $250.00. (3) Processor of industrial hemp fee - $500.00." That is an original (introduced) bill text, not enacted law as shown in that document, and it conflicts with the current LDAF/LAC $500-each practice. It is listed here only to prevent its accidental use: do not quote a $250 grower fee as current Louisiana law. Its final disposition is [VERIFY on legis.la.gov — SB 495 (2024) bill history]; secondary tracking (FastDemocracy, accessed 25 Oct 2026, https://fastdemocracy.com/bill/la/2024/bills/LAB00023405/) shows only introduction/referral steps in its summary and is not relied on for final status.

Licence term and renewal (LAC, opened directly): LAC 7:XIII §1305(C) (March 2026 compilation, same PDF, opened 25 Oct 2026): "The effective dates of all industrial hemp licenses shall be from the date of issuance through December 31 of any given year, and licenses must be renewed annually by November 30." LAC §1305 also provides: each licensee is assigned a licence number "in the form prescribed by the USDA"; applications are handled/processed by LDAF and the applicant is notified of approval or denial; "The licensee shall be responsible for the cost of all licenses and sample testing fees"; no unlicensed person who is not an employee of a licensee shall grow, cultivate, handle, store, process, or transport industrial hemp (employees do not include independent contractors or persons issued a 1099 by the licensee); no person under 18 shall be granted a licence; and a person applying for multiple licences must complete an application and submit the associated fee for each application. Change-of-information: LAC §1305(J) requires written requests for licence modification within 15 days of any change (mirroring R.S. 3:1465(C)(2)).

No cap, no minimum acreage (LDAF regulations page, opened 25 Oct 2026): "There is no limit to the number of licenses Louisiana issues, and there is no minimum number of production acres to be a licensed grower. You can grow industrial hemp plants in your yard as long as you're licensed." And: "Holders of Permanent Resident Cards (also known as Green Cards) are eligible for industrial hemp licenses."

Act 462 of 2022 — noted, not detailed: The LDAF regulations page links "Act 462 of the 2022 Regular Legislative Session" (legis.la.gov link on that page, opened 25 Oct 2026 via the regulations page). Its subject matter was not opened line-by-line in this run; it is listed here as a follow-up, not asserted as a hemp-licence change. [VERIFY — open Act 462 of 2022 and record its hemp effect, if any, before citing it.]

7.3 LDAF licences in detail — grower, processor (non-consumable), handler, seed producer

7.3.1 Grower Licence — LDAF

  • Allows (statute, verbatim): "possess, store, cultivate, trim, dry, cure, and transport industrial hemp in this state" — R.S. 3:1465(A)(2), legis.la.gov (opened 25 Oct 2026).
  • Allows (regulation, LAC §1309, March 2026 compilation, opened 25 Oct 2026): "A grower license issued by LDAF shall authorize the licensee to obtain industrial hemp seed, possess industrial hemp seed for planting, cultivate an industrial hemp crop, harvest industrial hemp plant parts, as well as possess, store, transport, and market plant parts grown under their grower's license pursuant to this Chapter."
  • Application must include (LAC §1309(C)): type of licence; applicant's full name, Louisiana mailing and physical address, telephone, email, proof of identification; for a business entity, business name, principal Louisiana business physical address, applicant individual's name/title/email, designated responsible party's name/title/email, registered agent's name/mailing address, and employer identification number; physical address, legal description, location ID, and GPS coordinates for each field, greenhouse, indoor growing structure, or site where hemp will be cultivated, handled, or stored; and detailed maps depicting each site with entrances, field boundaries, and GPS-corresponding locations, plus proposed field acreage or square footage.
  • Ongoing duties (LAC §1319, opened 25 Oct 2026): post a compliant sign at each field/greenhouse/indoor structure for the entire crop cycle (18" × 24" for a field, 8.5" × 11" for a greenhouse/indoor structure, at the main entrance, in LDAF's template design, showing "Louisiana Industrial Hemp Program," licence number, and LDAF programme telephone number); submit a first report of planting within 15 days of planting (and, for seed producers, quarterly reports — see §7.3.4); submit a Harvest or Destruction report within 15 days of the intended harvest/destruction date; do not harvest more than 30 days after LDAF sample collection unless LDAF authorises it in writing; report crop acreage/square footage to the USDA Farm Service Agency and provide LDAF the corresponding FSA 578 form with planting reports; destroy unharvested plants on crop failure or failure to harvest, by an LDAF-approved written method; monitor and destroy volunteer plants for three years after cultivation ends. LDAF representatives have "complete and unrestricted access" to plants, land, buildings, and structures used for cultivation, handling, or storage.
  • Fee / term: $500/year; term to 31 December; renew by 30 November (see §7.2).
  • Info link: https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp/hemp-licensing (opened 25 Oct 2026).

7.3.2 Processor Licence (non-consumable only) — LDAF

  • Allows (statute, verbatim): "possess, store, process, and transport industrial hemp in this state" — R.S. 3:1465(A)(3), legis.la.gov (opened 25 Oct 2026).
  • Allows (regulation, LAC §1311, March 2026 compilation, opened 25 Oct 2026): "A processor license issued by LDAF shall authorize the licensee to possess, process, store, or transport industrial hemp plant parts for processing pursuant to this Chapter." And: "No person shall process industrial hemp into a nonconsumable product without first applying for and receiving an industrial hemp processor license from LDAF."
  • Critical boundary — consumable processing is NOT under this licence: LDAF regulations page (opened 25 Oct 2026): "As a result of Act 336 of the 2021 Regular Legislative Session, LDAF is no longer authorized to license or regulate processors of 'consumable' hemp as defined by R.S. 3:1481. Anyone interested in processing consumable hemp should go through the Louisiana Department of Health." LAC Chapter 13's processor definition is consistent: a processor receives hemp "for processing into nonconsumable hemp commodities or products" and "shall not include a consumable hemp processor as defined in R.S. 3:1481" (LAC §1303 definition, as returned in search-index text — [VERIFY — open LAC §1303 directly for the verbatim definition]).
  • Application: Same common application contents as §7.3.1, with detailed maps, legal description, physical address, location ID, and GPS coordinates for each building/site where hemp will be cleaned, packaged, handled, or stored (LAC §1311(C), opened 25 Oct 2026).
  • Fee / term: $500/year; term to 31 December; renew by 30 November (see §7.2).
  • Info link: Same LDAF licensing page.

7.3.3 Handler Licence — LDAF (the transport licence in current law)

  • Allows (statute, verbatim): "handle industrial hemp in this state" — R.S. 3:1465(A)(4), legis.la.gov (opened 25 Oct 2026). The statute's single word "handle" is expanded by regulation.
  • Allows (regulation, LAC §1313(B), March 2026 compilation, opened 25 Oct 2026): "A handler license issued by LDAF shall authorize the licensee to: 1. transport or deliver industrial hemp in intrastate commerce for compensation; 2. commercially harvest, store, or grind industrial hemp material received from a grower;" plus, as returned in the same section, clean or package seed received from a seed producer, broker industrial hemp material, and receive industrial hemp for testing. The handler licence is therefore the current standalone transport-for-compensation licence. A grower, processor, or seed producer may transport their own material under their own licence (see §§7.3.1, 7.3.2, 7.3.4); a third party transporting another licensee's hemp for compensation needs the handler licence — that is the practical rule, stated here from the LAC text, not from the 2021 secondary Q&A that Run 1 did not adopt.
  • Application: Same common contents; handler-specific site information for buildings/sites where hemp will be handled/stored (LAC §1313(C), opened 25 Oct 2026).
  • Fee / term: $500/year; term to 31 December; renew by 30 November (see §7.2).
  • Info link: Same LDAF licensing page.
  • Historic contract carrier — superseded, do not apply for it today: The 2019–2020 statute and LDAF materials listed a fourth type, "contract carrier — authorizes the licensee to transport industrial hemp." The current R.S. 3:1465 (opened 25 Oct 2026) lists handler, not contract carrier, in (A)(4), and the current LDAF licensing page lists only Grower, Processor, Handler, and Seed Producer. Run 1 correctly treated the standalone contract-carrier type as historic/superseded. New tension found in this run: the LAC March 2026 compilation's §1303 definition of "Licensee" still reads "any person possessing a contract carrier, grower, processor or seed producer license issued by LDAF" (as returned in search-index text for that PDF). That definition appears stale against the current statute and the current LDAF page. [VERIFY — confirm with LDAF whether the LAC §1303 "contract carrier" reference is a leftover definition or a live licence class; do not apply for a "contract carrier" licence on the basis of that definition alone.] Historic counts using the old label are in §7.10.

7.3.4 Seed Producer Licence — LDAF

  • Allows (statute, verbatim): "produce, transport, and sell approved seeds to licensed industrial hemp growers, seed producers, handlers, and processors" and "A licensed seed producer shall ensure that the seed complies with the standards set by the commission" — R.S. 3:1465(A)(1), legis.la.gov (opened 25 Oct 2026). "The department shall provide information that identifies sellers of industrial hemp seed to growers" — same paragraph.
  • Allows (regulation, LAC §1307, March 2026 compilation, opened 25 Oct 2026): "A seed producer license issued by LDAF shall authorize the licensee to obtain, produce, transport, and sell industrial hemp seed pursuant to this Chapter." And: "No person shall produce industrial hemp seed for planting purposes without first applying for and being granted a seed producer license from LDAF." Seed producers must also comply with R.S. 3:1431 et seq. (Louisiana Seed Law), including testing and labelling of agricultural seeds.
  • Seed-specific duties (LAC §§1307, 1319, 1321, opened 25 Oct 2026): All industrial hemp seed produced in Louisiana must be certified true to type under the Louisiana seed certification programme for industrial hemp seed; no other industrial hemp seed may be produced in Louisiana for distribution or sale unless approved by LDAF; no person shall sell/transfer seed to any person in Louisiana without first verifying the recipient is licensed by LDAF, and no person shall buy/acquire seed from any person in Louisiana without first verifying the distributor is a seed producer or handler licensed by LDAF; seed acquisition from outside Louisiana requires a completed seed acquisition request form with attachments and LDAF written approval before acquisition (LAC §1321(A)); seed for planting must be accompanied by a third-party independent laboratory certificate of analysis showing THC not more than the acceptable level, a seed purity and germination analysis report (R.S. 3:1436), and a compliant seed label (R.S. 3:1436). Seed producers must file a first report of planting within 15 days of planting for true-seed production, and quarterly planting reports (by 31 March, 30 June, 30 September, 31 December) for vegetative stock plantings.
  • Variety designation: LDAF publishes the "LDAF Industrial Hemp Program Variety Designation List as of January 15, 2026" (linked from the LDAF regulations page and the LDAF seed-purchase page, accessed 25 Oct 2026). Varieties are designated not yet tested / non-designated / variety of concern / approved / prohibited, based on official LDAF test results; a variety is "prohibited" if, among other tests, more than 50% of official LDAF sample results are above 0.30% total THC, or any official result exceeds 1.0% total THC (LAC §1303, March 2026 compilation, opened 25 Oct 2026). The variety list itself is a designation list, not a licence.
  • Hemp seed certification standards (related, not a licence): LAC Title 7, Part XIII, Chapter 12 (§§1201–1209) sets hemp seed certification standards (general, hemp seed, feminized hemp seed, vegetatively propagated hemp seed, hemp transplants) — same March 2026 compilation, table of contents (opened 25 Oct 2026). Certification is a seed-quality programme; it does not replace the seed producer licence.
  • Fee / term: $500/year; term to 31 December; renew by 30 November (see §7.2).
  • Info links: https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp/hemp-licensing and https://www.ldaf.state.la.us/plants/industrial-hemp/purchase-transport (accessed 25 Oct 2026; the latter page states the seed, clone, and transplant provider list is "for informational purposes only … and includes licensed companies and individuals who have sent us their information. LDAF is not affiliated with and does not endorse any provider, and your options are not limited to this list").

7.4 Common LDAF requirements (all four LDAF licences)

  • One application, multiple licences: "You may apply for individual or multiple licenses on one application" — LDAF licensing page (opened 25 Oct 2026). LAC §1305(I): a person applying for multiple licences must complete an application and submit the associated fee for each application.
  • Before applying (LDAF licensing page, opened 25 Oct 2026): (1) Review the industrial hemp law, rules and regulations, and compliance checklist; (2) Complete your background check; (3) One state and federal background check report suffices for multiple licences if performed within 60 days of the date the application is received by LDAF; (4) Create a colour photographic map for each growing, storage, handling, or processing location.
  • Background check — who and how (statute + regulation): R.S. 3:1465(D) (opened 25 Oct 2026): applicant (applicant or designated responsible party, per R.S. 3:1462) submits fingerprints and identifying information to the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information for state and national criminal history; the bureau may charge a reasonable processing fee under R.S. 15:587(B), paid by the applicant; history not already public is nonpublic/confidential for LDAF eligibility use only. LAC §1315 (opened 25 Oct 2026): each seed producer, grower, processor, or handler applicant shall undergo and pay for a criminal background check under R.S. 3:1465(D); for a business entity, the individual applying and the designated responsible party shall undergo and pay for it; the report must be issued within 60 days before submission (LDAF shall not accept a report issued more than 60 days prior); substitution of a designated responsible party requires a current report issued within the last 60 days and prior LDAF written approval.
  • Disqualifications (verbatim, R.S. 3:1465(D)(5), opened 25 Oct 2026): "No person shall be eligible to obtain a license if convicted under state or federal law of any of the following: (a) A felony within the ten years immediately preceding the date of application. (b) A drug-related misdemeanor within the two years immediately preceding the date of application." LAC §1305(H) adds ineligibility for failure to provide all application requirements/documentation or material falsification of the application.
  • Age: "No person under the age of 18 years of age shall be granted a license under this Chapter" — LAC §1305(G) (opened 25 Oct 2026).
  • Responsibility for employees: "The applicant is responsible for any employee working under the applicant's license" — R.S. 3:1465(E) (opened 25 Oct 2026). LAC §1305(F) excludes independent contractors and 1099 persons from "employee" for this purpose.
  • Site changes: Complete a Site Modification Request (online form or PDF form linked from the LDAF licensing page, opened 25 Oct 2026) or, for a designated responsible party change, a new Designated Responsible Party Declaration. LAC §1305(J): written modification requests within 15 days of any change.
  • Research exemption: R.S. 3:1465(F) (opened 25 Oct 2026) exempts LSU AgCenter, Southern University AgCenter, University of Louisiana at Monroe Agribusiness Program, and University of Louisiana at Monroe College of Pharmacy "when performing research and development as provided for in R.S. 3:1469." That exemption is for research and development; it is not a commercial grower/processor licence and does not authorise commercial sale. [VERIFY — open R.S. 3:1469 for the exact scope of the research exemption before relying on it.]
  • Testing and harvest window (LAC §§1317, 1319, opened 25 Oct 2026): THC testing $250 per sample, due at sample collection; a crop shall not be harvested more than 30 days after LDAF sample collection unless LDAF authorises it in writing; LDAF may sample/test any licensee material at any time if it has reason to believe a violation occurred. (Run 1 Part 1/Part 11 context: pre-harvest sampling is the compliance gate; this run does not re-do Part 11 operations rules in full.)

7.5 LDH consumable hemp processor permit — in-state facility

  • Statute and verbatim fee schedule (legis.la.gov, opened 25 Oct 2026, R.S. 3:1483(A)(1)):

"Each consumable hemp processor shall obtain an annual consumable hemp processor permit issued by the department. The department shall charge and collect an annual consumable hemp processor permit fee. The fee shall be for each separate processing facility and shall be based on the annual sales of such facility according to the following schedule: Annual Sales / Annual Fee — Under $500,000 / $175.00; $500,001 - $1,000,000 / $475.00; $1,000,001 - $2,500,000 / $775.00; $2,500,001 - $5,000,000 / $1,075.00; Over $5,000,000 / $1,375.00"

  • Additional statutory requirements (same R.S. 3:1483(A)(2)–(6), opened 25 Oct 2026): In addition to R.S. 3:1485 qualifications, the applicant must meet LDH rules for the physical processing facility and equipment; conduct a potency test of the distillate or concentrate used; conduct a test on each batch showing (a) disaggregated THC components by percentage of total THC, (b) serving size of an individual unit, (c) total THC milligrams per serving, and (d) presence and concentration of solvents, pesticides, microbials, and heavy metals; retain each test record for a minimum of three years; and adhere to LDH sanitary regulations.
  • Out-of-state product exception (same section, opened 25 Oct 2026): "A permitted consumable hemp processor may produce consumable hemp products that exceed the allowable total THC per serving and package size required for product approval in Paragraph (B)(6) of this Section if" the holder completes a sworn written statement that the product will be delivered/transported beyond Louisiana's borders and meets the receiving state/territory's requirements, conducts the same distillate/concentrate tests, and maintains the sworn statement and distinct distribution records (batch ID, product name, receiving state/territory) for a minimum of three years — R.S. 3:1483(A)(7). This is an export permission, not a permission to sell over-limit products in Louisiana.
  • What the permit does NOT do on its own: It does not register any product. Each product still needs LDH registration and label approval (§7.7), and retail/wholesale sale still needs an ATC permit (§§7.8–7.11).
  • Info link: https://ldh.la.gov/page/hemp-registration (opened 25 Oct 2026). The LDH primer (Run 1, 2023) also describes an in-state "Permit to Operate" with the LDH Food and Drug Unit for facilities manufacturing consumable hemp for ingestion, under Act 498 of 2022 authority — see the §7.0 table; whether that Permit to Operate is the same instrument as the R.S. 3:1483 processor permit or a separate facility permit, and whether it carries a separate fee, was not resolved in this run. [VERIFY — ask LDH Food and Drug Unit whether a separate Permit to Operate fee applies in addition to the R.S. 3:1483 tier fee.]

7.6 LDH consumable hemp processor permit — out-of-state processor, and the Act 752 sponsorship rule

  • Act 752 rule (LDH page, opened 25 Oct 2026):

"NOTE: Due to changes resulting from Act 752 of the 2024 Regular Legislature, any consumable hemp product to be registered must be submitted through a permitted in-state hemp products processor OR a permitted out-of-state hemp processor. A list of in-state firms that may sponsor out-of-state products may be found here."

  • Out-of-state application contents (same LDH page, opened 25 Oct 2026): an application fee of $175 ("fees are based on a sliding scale but the department will assess additional fees if applicable at a later point in time"); FD-99a application form; list of stakeholders having more than a 5% stake with percentages; notarised attestation of good character of the major stakeholders — specifically that the natural persons have not been convicted of a felony by the U.S. or any state/territory, or of soliciting for prostitution, pandering, letting premises for prostitution, contributing to delinquency of juveniles, keeping/letting a disorderly place, or illegally dealing in controlled dangerous substances; sole proprietors must also supply a state-issued photo ID showing date of birth.
  • How this differs from the in-state tier fee: The LDH page states the $175 figure as an application fee for the out-of-state route and warns additional fees may be assessed later on a sliding scale. It does not on the page text opened state that the out-of-state final fee equals the in-state tier fee. Do not equate them without LDH confirmation. [VERIFY — LDH out-of-state processor final fee schedule.]
  • Sponsor list: The LDH page's "list of in-state firms that may sponsor out-of-state products" link was not opened as a list in this run (the page text returned does not reproduce the list). Run 1 Part 5 §5.3 recorded the same gap. [VERIFY — open the sponsor list from the LDH hemp registration page and record its URL, date, and firm count.]
  • General permit-holder qualifications (R.S. 3:1485, as returned in a legis.la.gov amendment document — [VERIFY current text]): The House floor amendments document for SB 237 (legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1381220, accessed 25 Oct 2026) reproduces §1485 as: "An applicant for any permit issued pursuant to this Part shall demonstrate that he meets all of the following requirements: (1) Be a person of good character and reputation and over the age of twenty-one. (2) Has not been convicted of distributing or possessing with the intent to distribute any controlled dangerous substance classified in Schedule I of R.S. 40:964, on any premises permitted pursuant to this Part, where the applicant held or holds an interest in the permitted business. (3) Has not been convicted of a felony under the laws of the United States, the state of Louisiana, or any other state or country." That document is an amendment document, not the enrolled Act 752 text and not the current legis.la.gov law page for §1485, so the §1485 text above is flagged [VERIFY against current R.S. 3:1485 on legis.la.gov] and must not be quoted as current official text until that check is done. The LDH out-of-state good-character attestation above is consistent with a felony bar, but it is not a substitute for the §1485 text.

7.7 LDH consumable hemp product registration (per product) — FD-8a

This is a registration, not a business licence, but it is the gate for every consumable hemp product sold for Louisiana use, so it is inventoried here in full. It is distinct from the processor permit (§§7.5–7.6): the processor is permitted; each product is registered.

  • Statute (legis.la.gov, opened 25 Oct 2026, R.S. 3:1483(B)): "Any consumable hemp product that is manufactured, distributed, imported, or sold for use in Louisiana shall meet the following criteria: (1) Be produced from hemp grown by a licensee authorized to grow hemp by the United States Department of Agriculture or under an approved state plan pursuant to the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018, P.L. 115-334, or under an authorized state pilot program pursuant to the Agriculture Act of 2014, P.L. 113-79. (2) Be registered with the department in accordance with the provisions of this Section. The department shall charge and collect a fee of not more than fifty dollars for each separate and distinct product registered. This charge shall be in lieu of the charge collected pursuant to R.S. 40:628. (3) Receive product and label approval from the department. (4) Not be marketed as dietary. (5) Not contain any active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) recognized by the United States Food and Drug Administration other than cannabidiol [topical exception in the same paragraph]. (6) Individual servings and packages [must meet the 5 mg / 40 mg, beverage, and tincture limits carried from Run 1 — see §0]."
  • Label approval — what LDH will not approve (same section, opened 25 Oct 2026, R.S. 3:1483(C)(2)): floral hemp material for retail sale; any inhalable consumable hemp product, including vapes (with a "not for inhalation" label not curing an inhalation design); any alcoholic beverage regulated by ATC that contains consumable hemp; any product packaged in a manner more appealing to children (including a name/logo/mascot similar to a non-consumable hemp candy or beverage product); and any product not complying with Subsection B. Labels must contain no medical claims; have a scannable bar code, QR code, or web address linked to a certificate of analysis; clearly state total THC per serving; warn that THC consumption may result in a failed drug test; and accurately reflect contents within a 15% variance (R.S. 3:1483(C)(1), opened 25 Oct 2026).
  • Certificate of analysis (same section, opened 25 Oct 2026, R.S. 3:1483(E)–(F)): The application must include a CoA certifying batch ID, product name, date received, date of completion, and method of analysis; test results for solvents, pesticides, microbials, and heavy metals; cannabinoid profile by percentage of weight; and a final-product potency test showing serving size, total THC per serving, total servings, and total THC per package (in mg/g units as stated). The CoA must be completed by an independent laboratory accredited by ISO or another LDH-approved accrediting entity, approved by LDH, with no direct or indirect interest in a grower, processor, wholesaler, or retailer of hemp products. The University of Louisiana at Monroe-affiliated laboratory is the preferred laboratory once it meets all requirements and commences operations; processors may use any other laboratory meeting the requirements.
  • LDH process (LDH page, opened 25 Oct 2026): Upload to the portal: labels for each product; CoAs from accredited labs for each product; completed FD-10 application form for each product; laboratory accreditation verification (ISO-IEC 17025); attestation the product was produced from hemp; photographs/renderings of each product including accessories; detailed written description of how individual servings will be packaged/marketed; complete list of the firm's previously registered products. "Products will not be registered until every document (with correct information as required by LDH) is submitted to the portal." Each time LDH asks for more documentation, and upon each response, the 60-day period to register or decline begins anew (60 business days, excluding weekends, legal holidays, and state office closures); if LDH requests more information and hears nothing within 60 business days, LDH will close the file. "Administrative Coordinators will send an invoice ($50 per product submitted for registration) once every product has been accepted for registration," payable by money order, cashier's check, or online through the portal, payable to LDH. On registration, the product is placed on the "Louisiana Department of Health Database for Registered Consumable Hemp Products" and the applicant receives a Certificate of Consumable Hemp Product Registration (FD-8a). "Each product must be renewed between July 1 and August 15 of every year"; with LDH permission, a firm may attest/certify the product has not changed in lieu of repeat submission.
  • Statutory 60-day sale-pending rule (same R.S. 3:1483(G)(1), opened 25 Oct 2026) — note the tension with the LDH page: "The department shall: (1) Conduct an initial review of any product submitted pursuant to this Section and notify the submitting party of any deficiencies … within sixty business days of the date of submission. If the department fails to notify the submitting party within sixty business days of the date of submission, the product may be sold by a wholesaler or retailer permitted pursuant to R.S. 3:1484 from the day following the sixtieth business day until the submitting party receives final approval or denial from the department for the product." The LDH page's "clock resets on each request" description and the statute's "initial review within 60 business days" description are not identical; Run 1 Part 4 §4.4.3 recorded the same tension (and an older 15-business-day rule excerpt). This run does not resolve it: do not advise a seller that a product may be sold on day 61 on the basis of either text alone — [VERIFY the current LDH rule (LAC 49:I §517) and LDH's current portal guidance together].
  • "Louisiana Hemp Product" designation: R.S. 3:1483(G)(5) (opened 25 Oct 2026) requires LDH to develop a process to register a product grown and processed in Louisiana as a "Louisiana Hemp Product" (with a possible logo); no product may hold itself out as a "Louisiana Hemp Product" unless registered under that process and rules. Whether the designation process/logo is currently operational was not confirmed in this run. [VERIFY.]
  • Fee: $50 per product, per the LDH page and the "not more than fifty dollars" statutory cap above. Renewal fee is the same $50 figure on the LDH page's invoicing description; the statute's "in lieu of R.S. 40:628" language is the authority for not charging the general food/drug examination charge in addition.
  • Info link: https://ldh.la.gov/page/hemp-registration (opened 25 Oct 2026). Public database URL: the LDH page names the "Louisiana Department of Health Database for Registered Consumable Hemp Products" but the page text opened does not give a separate public database URL; the legacy URL on the ATC wholesale form (https://ldh.la.gov/index.cfm/page/4081) was not opened successfully as a current database in Run 1 and was not re-opened successfully in this run. [VERIFY — current public database URL and whether it offers export/download.] See §7.10.

7.8 ATC consumable hemp permits — wholesaler, retailer, remote retailer, special event

  • Governing statute: R.S. 3:1484, "Permit to sell; office of alcohol and tobacco control." Current-text caveat: The current legis.la.gov law page for R.S. 3:1484 was not returned in this run. The verbatim passages below are from Justia's 2022 republication, https://law.justia.com/codes/louisiana/2022/revised-statutes/title-3/rs-3-1484/ (accessed 25 Oct 2026), and from the ATC law book PDF, https://atc.louisiana.gov/media/mkjnhupd/law-book.pdf (accessed 25 Oct 2026, whose §1483/§1484 excerpts pre-date Act 752 in the text returned). Every §1484 passage below is therefore [VERIFY against current R.S. 3:1484 on legis.la.gov, as amended by Act 752 of 2024 and any later Act] before being quoted as current law. The Act 752 location bans (gasoline, bar/restaurant) are stated separately below from ATC's own advisory, which is current and primary for that point.
  • Wholesaler (Justia 2022 text, accessed 25 Oct 2026):

"A.(1) Each wholesaler of consumable hemp products shall apply for and obtain a permit from the office of alcohol and tobacco control." "(2) The commissioner may establish and collect an annual wholesaler permit fee. The amount of the wholesaler permit fee shall be based on the cost of the regulatory functions performed and shall not exceed five hundred dollars per year."

  • Wholesaler — amount actually charged (ATC form, accessed 25 Oct 2026): "Consumable Hemp Wholesale Application Fee $500.00" and "all application and permit fees are nonrefundable" — ATC wholesale application form, https://atc.louisiana.gov/media/idcpj45s/application-for-consumable-hemp-wholesale-permit_a11y.pdf. Form file name as in URL: application-for-consumable-hemp-wholesale-permit_a11y.pdf. "Wholesaler" means "a wholesale seller, distributor, or packer of consumable hemp products" (same form). Checklist on the same form: coloured copy of driver's licence for each owner/member/director/officer; corporate documents (articles as filed with the Secretary of State, notarised partnership agreement, etc.); proof of registration and good standing with the Louisiana Secretary of State; Louisiana Tax Clearance certificate from the Department of Revenue; application fees. Submission: ATC online licensing system, https://laatcabc.atc.la.gov/laatcprod/pub/Login.aspx, or by mail to 7979 Independence Blvd., Suite 101, Baton Rouge, LA 70896-6404 / P.O. Box 66404, Baton Rouge, LA 70896, or in person at ATC offices (same form; ATC public telephone on the form is (225) 925-4041 — official public contact, reproduced here because it is on the public form).
  • Retailer (Justia 2022 text, accessed 25 Oct 2026):

"B.(1)(a) Each person who sells or is about to engage in the business of selling at retail any consumable hemp product shall first apply for and obtain a permit for each place of business from the office of alcohol and tobacco control." "(b) For purposes of this Section, each individually registered domain name owned or leased by or on behalf of a remote retailer shall be considered a place of business. No person or entity shall be required to have a physical place of business in the state of Louisiana in order to sell consumable hemp products at retail." "(2) Prior to selling consumable hemp products at a special event, the retailer shall request and promptly receive an annual special event permit from the commissioner. For purposes of this Section, a special event shall be defined as any event held at any location, other than a permitted place of business, where consumable hemp products are sold. The permittee shall notify the commissioner in writing of any special event the permittee will be attending prior to the event. Failure to notify the commissioner shall be grounds for revocation of the permit." "(3) No permit issued pursuant to this Section shall authorize the permittee to sell or offer for sale any cannabinoid product derived from any source other than hemp."

  • Retail / special-event fee cap (Justia 2022 text, accessed 25 Oct 2026): "The commissioner may establish and collect an annual retail permit fee and an annual special event permit fee. The amount of each permit fee … shall be based on the cost of the regulatory functions performed and shall not exceed one hundred seventy-five dollars per year." Amount actually charged — [VERIFY]: Run 1 recorded the $175 figure as a statutory cap with the actual charged fee unverified, because the ATC retail form was not opened. In this run, a secondary source (Crescent Canna, "Last Chance for Louisiana Bars & Restaurants," accessed 25 Oct 2026, https://www.crescentcanna.com/lra/) states for the 2024–2025 permit year: "The permit costs $175 and is valid from April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2025." That is secondary and dated; it corroborates the cap but does not confirm the current (2026–2027) retail/special-event fee. Do not quote "$175" as the current charged retail fee without opening the current ATC retail application or ATC fee schedule. A separate secondary compilation (lahemp.net, accessed 25 Oct 2026, https://lahemp.net/sitecore/content/lih/obtaining-licenses) also states "$175.00 per a permit" for retail/special-event dealer permits and lists four ATC dealer permit types (retail dealer, remote seller, wholesaler, special event dealer) — again secondary, used here only to show the four-type structure is consistently described, not as a fee confirmation.
  • Remote retailer — definition (ATC wholesale form, accessed 25 Oct 2026): "Remote retailer means a person or entity who offers any consumable hemp product for sale at retail or for any transaction of products in lieu of a sale, through digital application, catalog, or the internet, that can be purchased and delivered directly to a consumer in Louisiana." Department of Revenue FAQ (accessed 25 Oct 2026, https://revenue.louisiana.gov/tax-education-and-faqs/faqs/excise-taxes/consumable-hemp-products/do-i-have-to-have-a-permit-to-sell-consumable-hemp-products/): "Retailers must obtain a license for each place of business and each individually registered domain name owned or leased by or on behalf of a remote consumable hemp product retailer." No Louisiana physical place of business is required for a remote retailer on the face of §1484(B)(1)(b) above.
  • Bars and restaurants — no NEW permits (ATC advisory, primary, accessed 25 Oct 2026): ATC Advisory, 5 June 2024, https://atc.louisiana.gov/media/aykoohit/24-06-05_advisory_retail-hemp-permits-for-bars-and-restaurants.pdf: "Under HB 952, ATC will discontinue the issuance of any new hemp retail permits for any business that is also licensed as a bar or restaurant (Class AR or AG permit)." And: the deadline discussed in that advisory "is NOT intended to allow bars and restaurants which do not currently hold a hemp retail permit to apply now" and an application "not reviewed and approved before the deadline date … will be denied in accordance with law. Any applications fees submitted to the ATC are nonrefundable." This is the Act 752 (HB 952) bar/restaurant rule in ATC's own words; the underlying Act 752 location prohibitions (including the gasoline/motor-fuel retail location ban with the R.S. 27:417 qualified truck-stop exemption) are carried from Run 1 Part 1 §1.6 / Part 4 §4.4.4 and are not re-quoted here.
  • Retailer sourcing rule — [VERIFY]: Run 1 Part 4 §4.4.4 recorded, from a House floor amendment document (not the enrolled Act 752 text), a rule that a retailer must obtain consumable hemp products only from an ATC-permitted wholesaler. That rule is not confirmed in this run against current R.S. 3:1484 and remains [VERIFY].
  • Proposed retail-fee increase — do NOT use as law: A 2023 engrossed bill (HB 605, legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1314368, accessed 25 Oct 2026) proposed: "The annual retail permit fee shall not exceed two hundred fifty dollars and the annual special event permit fee shall not exceed one hundred seventyfive dollars per year." That is a proposed engrossed text. Do not quote a $250 retail cap as current law; the $175 cap in the 2022 §1484 text above is the last verified statutory cap in this run, itself subject to the Act 752 re-check.
  • Revocation / tax-suspension mechanism — [VERIFY current text]: The SB 237 House floor amendments document (legis.la.gov, https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=1381220, accessed 25 Oct 2026) reproduces a §1484(F) mechanism under which the Secretary of Revenue shall order ATC to immediately suspend a retailer's permit if the retailer fails to timely file returns or pay taxes under R.S. 47:1693, until returns are filed and taxes paid (with protested/appealed taxes excepted). Because that document is an amendment document, not current law text, the mechanism is listed here as [VERIFY against current R.S. 3:1484] and is not asserted as current law.

7.9 Other hemp authorisations, non-licences, and what was searched for and not found

  • No standalone transporter / distributor / importer licence (current): No separate LDAF "transporter" licence exists on the current LDAF licensing page; transport is within the grower, processor, handler, and seed producer licences (§§7.3.1–7.3.4), with handler as the for-compensation transport licence. No separate "distributor" licence was located; distribution of consumable hemp products is covered by the ATC wholesaler permit (§7.8). No separate "importer" licence was located; an imported consumable product must still be produced from USDA/state-plan hemp, registered with LDH through a permitted processor, and sold by an ATC-permitted wholesaler/retailer (R.S. 3:1483(B)(1), opened 25 Oct 2026). If a future source shows a distinct importer permit, it should be added here — its absence in this run is a searched absence, not a proof of non-existence beyond the sources opened.
  • No hemp testing-laboratory licence (as a licence type): Consumable hemp testing is by ISO-accredited independent laboratories approved by LDH (R.S. 3:1483(F), opened 25 Oct 2026), with UL Monroe as the preferred laboratory once operational and approved. LDAF's own laboratory (5825 Florida Boulevard, Baton Rouge) is one of the 3 LDH-approved medical testing laboratories in Run 1 Part 4 §4.3, but that is a medical-lab approval, not a hemp-lab licence. No standalone "hemp testing laboratory licence" with a fee schedule was located. [VERIFY — whether LDH maintains a published list of approved consumable-hemp testing laboratories distinct from the medical lab list.]
  • No hemp retailer licence from LDAF or LDH: Retail is ATC only (see §7.8). Run 1 Part 4 §4.4.5 recorded the same point.
  • Seed dealer overlay (not a hemp licence): The LDAF Industrial Hemp Seed Acquisition Request form (form AES-28-08, R.2/20, via https://storage.googleapis.com/stateless-valhalla/2022/02/482e220b-la-seed-acquisition-request-form.pdf, accessed 25 Oct 2026 — a dated form copy, not the live LDAF form) states: "Distributors of industrial hemp seed must possess a current Louisiana Seed Dealer License." That requirement is therefore recorded as a form-stated overlay [VERIFY — confirm the current seed dealer licence requirement, issuing division, and fee on the current LDAF Seed Programs pages], not as a current hemp licence type. It matters because a seed producer who also distributes seed to other licensees may need both the hemp seed producer licence and the seed dealer licence.
  • "Louisiana Hemp Product" designation: See §7.7 — a designation process, not a licence; operational status [VERIFY].
  • Medical licences are not hemp licences: The 2 medical cultivation licences, 10 medical retail permits (plus satellites), and 3 medical testing laboratory approvals (Run 1 Part 4) are therapeutic-marijuana authorisations under R.S. 40:1046. They do not authorise any hemp activity, and no hemp licence authorises therapeutic marijuana activity. The proposed adult-use pilot (HB 373, 2026, Run 1 Part 4 §4.7) would have used only the existing medical permit holders and cultivators; it is PROPOSED only and creates no hemp or adult-use licence type.
  • Federal hemp dates — licence-holder impact (carried, not resolved): After 11 December 2026, on the given baseline, the federal hemp definition narrows to the full total-THC definition with a 0.4 mg total THC per container cap. A Louisiana LDH-registered product at the Louisiana limit (5 mg/serving, 40 mg/package) would therefore be outside the federal hemp definition while remaining Louisiana-lawful as written (Run 1 Part 1 §1.6.10). What that means for a Louisiana processor permit, product registration, or ATC permit — whether LDH/ATC will amend, suspend, or grandfather registrations, or whether interstate shipment of a Louisiana-registered product becomes federally unlawful — was not answered by any Louisiana agency source located in Run 1 or in this run. [UNAVAILABLE — re-check LDH, ATC, LDAF, and Governor/legislative sources after 11 December 2026; do not advise a licence holder that its Louisiana permit alone protects interstate shipment after that date.] The same caution applies to USDA DEA-lab testing enforcement delayed to 31 December 2026: Louisiana's pre-harvest testing is by LDAF (see §7.4), and no Louisiana statement adopting or rejecting the DEA-lab requirement for state-plan testing was located in this run.

8.0 Headline finding — no verifiably listed Louisiana cannabis-zoned property was found

In one line: on the sources searched and opened on 25 October 2026, there is no Louisiana property that can be listed here with a verified address, cannabis/hemp zoning or marketing claim, price, and active/recent listing status.

That is a searched negative, not an assertion that no such property exists anywhere in Louisiana. It means:

  1. The specialist cannabis-property platform for Louisiana returns zero listings when opened directly (see §8.1).
  2. The generic Louisiana city/category pages on the same platform return zero Louisiana listings and only generic marketing text plus out-of-state "spotlight" listings (see §8.1).
  3. General commercial-property and business-for-sale searches returned no Louisiana-specific cannabis/hemp listing with a verifiable address and price in this run; the items returned were out-of-state listings, general (non-cannabis) Louisiana commercial property, or address-number coincidences (see §§8.2–8.3).
  4. The structural reason is consistent with Run 1: Louisiana has no adult-use market, a closed medical system (2 producers, 10 retail permits, no new non-satellite permits), and a hemp market that operates through general commercial/industrial/agricultural property plus agency permits — not through a Louisiana "cannabis zone" or cannabis-specific zoning overlay that was located (see §8.4).

Because no Louisiana listing meeting the criteria was found, no property table with prices is presented. 8.4 Why Louisiana has (effectively) no cannabis-zoned property market to list — structural explanation

This section explains the negative finding; it does not create a listing.

  • No adult-use zoning market exists. Louisiana has no enacted adult-use law (Run 1 §0), so there is no adult-use retail, cultivation, or consumption zoning category to list, and no adult-use licence that a property could be "zoned for." The proposed adult-use pilot (HB 373, 2026) would have used only the existing 10 medical retail permit holders and 2 cultivators (Run 1 Part 4 §4.7) — it would not have created a new property class, and it is PROPOSED only.
  • Medical property is permit-bound, not zoning-bound. A medical retail location exists because LDH issued (or, for a satellite, notified and allowed) a permit holder to open it in a region, subject to state spacing (15/10/5 miles, R.S. 40:1046(G)(6), Run 1 Part 4 §4.2.1) — not because a parish zoned a parcel "cannabis." New non-satellite permits are closed ("No new permits may be issued for non-satellite locations at this time," LDH page, Run 1 Part 4 §4.2.3), and a new permit holder is selected by competitive bid only if a permit is revoked or voluntarily returned (R.S. 40:1046(G)(1)(c), Run 1 Part 4 §4.2.3). A property cannot therefore be marketed as "buy this parcel and open a new medical dispensary" in Louisiana, and no such marketing was found.
  • Membership-interest transfer is not a property listing. R.S. 40:1046(G)(1)(d) provides: "The transfer of a membership interest in an entity that holds a marijuana retail permit may be conducted without approval of the department" (Run 1 Part 4 §4.2.3). That means an ownership interest in a permit-holding entity can change hands without LDH approval, but it is not a real-estate listing, it does not transfer a parcel, and no such interest offering with a Louisiana address and price was verified in this run. Do not present a membership-interest transfer as a property sale.
  • Hemp property is general property + a licence. An LDAF grower licence has no minimum acreage and no cap (LDAF regulations page, §7.2), so hemp cultivation can in principle occur on ordinary agricultural land, a yard, a greenhouse, or an indoor structure if licensed and mapped — but the land itself is not "cannabis-zoned." A consumable hemp processor needs an LDH-permitted facility (per-facility permit, §7.5) and a retailer needs an ATC permit per place of business/domain (§7.8), but neither permit creates a zoning category. No Louisiana parish or city "cannabis zoning overlay" or "cannabis zone" ordinance was located in this run's searches. [VERIFY — targeted Municode/code search for "cannabis," "marijuana," and "hemp" in the New Orleans Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance, East Baton Rouge Unified Development Code, Lafayette, and Shreveport codes before asserting that no such overlay exists anywhere in Louisiana.]
  • Parish/city zoning still matters for siting, even without a cannabis zone: Run 1 Part 3 established that parishes, consolidated governments, and municipalities control generally applicable zoning, building/fire rules, and local occupational licences, but cannot create state permits or change state caps, and no parish-wide ban, moratorium, or cap was located in the 15 jurisdictions checked. A buyer of general commercial/industrial/agricultural property in Louisiana would still need to confirm, for that specific parcel, (a) the parish/city zoning allows the intended use, (b) any state spacing rule (medical) or location ban (consumable hemp: gasoline, bar/restaurant — see §7.8) does not bar it, and (c) the relevant state licence/permit can be held for that activity at that location. None of those parcel-specific checks could be performed here because no candidate parcel was verified.

Those anchors are: medical only, no adult-use law; LDH regulates (production/labs under Acts 491/492 of 2022 effective 1 August 2022, retailers from the Board of Pharmacy to LDH under Act 693 of 2024 effective 1 January 2025); Act 150 of 2024 transferred the 2 cultivation licences on 1 July 2024 to Good Day Farm Louisiana LLC and Advanced Biomedics LLC dba Ilera Holistic Healthcare, with a 1 July 2030 sunset; 10 base pharmacy permits + 19 satellites listed on the LDH page opened 25 October 2026 (29 locations), $22,500/year retail, $100,000/year cultivation + 7% gross-sales fee; no patient card/registry, clinician discretion, flower 71 g/14 days, no home grow, ≤14 g fine-only ≤$100; consumable hemp under Act 752 of 2024 effective 1 January 2025 — 5 mg total THC/serving, 40 mg/package, beverages 5 mg in ≥12 oz, age 21+, LDH registration + ATC permits; medical marijuana exempt from state AND local sales tax, consumable hemp excise 3%. Where a source found in this run contradicts a Run 1 anchor, the contradiction is flagged in §10.3 and in the Gaps list as a CONFLICT and Run 1 is NOT silently overwritten.

Federal baseline (given, NOT re-researched in this run): State-licensed medical marijuana and FDA-approved products moved to Schedule III effective 28 April 2026 (91 FR 22714); adult-use marijuana remains Schedule I; IRS §280E is generally lifted for Schedule III medical activity only; hemp PL 119-37 §781 takes effect 12 November 2026, but PL 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026, after which the full total-THC hemp definition and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply; USDA DEA-registered-lab hemp testing enforcement is delayed to 31 December 2026; the federal medical marijuana appropriations rider runs through 11 December 2026; there is no federal cannabis banking law. Nothing found in this run contradicts that baseline. Note for tribal/interstate analysis: Schedule III as given covers state-licensed medical activity; it does not, on its own, create a tribal or interstate medical-marijuana commerce regime, and no Louisiana tribal or interstate cannabis compact was located in this run (see §10.1.5 and §10.2.6).

Sourcing method note — read first: Official pages opened and read directly in this run: LDH Medical Marijuana page, LDH Hemp Registration page, LDAF Industrial Hemp page, ATC home page, Louisiana Board of Pharmacy Authorized Clinicians page, Governor's Office of Indian Affairs tribal list (PDF, updated 22 January 2024), and the USDA List of USDA-approved Hemp Plans page (updated 17 February 2026). Other statutes are quoted from legis.la.gov documents or Justia republications of the Louisiana Laws where the legis.la.gov law page itself could not be opened in full in this window; those items are cited to the source actually read and flagged [VERIFY] for a current legis.la.gov re-check before any verbatim text is relied on as current official text. Secondary sources (news, polls, law-firm and industry summaries) are used only for non-law facts and are labelled as such with publication dates, and must not be upgraded to law. No personal phone numbers or emails of individuals are reproduced; agency and tribal-government public contact details already published by those bodies are reproduced. Louisiana has parishes, not counties; "parish" is used throughout.

Agency Current cannabis/hemp role (Run 1-consistent) Historic / former role
Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), Office of Public Health, Bureau of Sanitarian Services, Cannabis Program Lead regulator of the medical (therapeutic) marijuana programme since 1 Aug 2022 (production, labs); of marijuana retailers since 1 Jan 2025; LDH registers consumable hemp products and permits consumable hemp processors (in-state and out-of-state) —
Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry (LDAF) Licences and regulates non-consumable industrial hemp (grower, processor, handler, seed producer); also runs the state hemp plan; its Baton Rouge laboratory is one of the 3 LDH-approved medical-marijuana testing laboratories Former medical-marijuana production regulator (before Acts 491/492 of 2022); former consumable-hemp processor regulator (before Act 336 of 2021)

9.1.1 Louisiana Department of Health (LDH) — lead regulator

  • What it does now (verbatim, LDH page): "Per Act 491 and Act 492 of the 2022 Regular Legislature, as of August 1, 2022, the Louisiana Department of Health has assumed regulatory authority over Louisiana's medical (therapeutic) marijuana program. LDH personnel are responsible for conducting inspections of medical marijuana production facilities and reviewing finished product test results to verify compliance with the requirements of La. R.S. 40: 1046." — LDH Medical Marijuana page, https://ldh.la.gov/page/medical-marijuana (accessed 25 Oct 2026).
  • Retailer transfer (verbatim, same page): "Act 693 of the 2024 Regular Legislature transferred authority over marijuana retailers from the Louisiana Board of Pharmacy to the Louisiana Department of Health. LDH's Cannabis Program began regulating these retail sites on January 1, 2025." — same source.
  • Programme home: Office of Public Health, Bureau of Sanitarian Services, Cannabis Program. The LDH page lists, in order: "Medical Marijuana Final Rule - published January 2026"; "Medical Marijuana Notice of Intent - published May 2025"; "Medical Marijuana Emergency Rule - promulgated March 28, 2025"; "Potpourri amending the proposed rules, published January 2025"; "Notice of Intent for Act 693 of 2024"; "Medical Marijuana Regulation - final rule published by the department in December 2022"; "Act 150 of the 2024 Legislature - extended the sunset date of the medical marijuana program to 2030, changed the basis for calculating patient numbers for reporting purposes, and removed the universities from the manufacturing program"; "Act 693 of the 2024 Legislature"; "Act 491 of the 2022 Legislature (also see Act 492 and Act 628)"; "Act 492 of the 2022 Legislature"; "Act 628 of the 2022 Legislature"; and a link to R.S. 40:1046 with the warning that "this online version has not yet been updated with 2024 changes" — all on the LDH page (accessed 25 Oct 2026).   • Current role (verbatim, LDAF page): "Produce, process, sell, and transport non-consumable hemp in Louisiana" and "The 2018 Farm Bill legalized the commercial production of hemp and authorized states to submit plans to administer hemp programs." — LDAF Industrial Hemp page, https://www.ldaf.la.gov/plants/industrial-hemp (accessed 25 Oct 2026).
